label: thm:main-collapse
statement: Let $m>n\ge2$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item The variety $Z$ is not normal, so RH in GCT VI, Theorem~7.6.6, is false. \item For $m\ge3$, the stretching function at $\lambda=(m-1,1)$ and $d=1$ is \[ a_m(k(m-1,1),k)=[z^k]\prod_{i=2}^{m}(1-z^i)^{-1}. \] It has degree $m-2$. Hence determinant-side PH1 cannot have its stated encoding bound uniform in $m$, polynomial in $n$ and the bit lengths of $m,d,\lambda$. \item Suppose that rational polytopes count the two stretched multiplicities, even only for all sufficiently large stretches. If $n\ge5$ and $m\ge n^{25}$, no robust obstruction exists. The same conclusion holds for $n\ge2$ and $m\ge(n+1)^{25}$. \item The determinant rays \[ \begin{gathered} (m,d,\lambda)=(3,4,(7,5)),\ (4,5,(11,9)),\\ (5,6,(15,15)),\ (6,7,(21,21)) \end{gathered} \] are not Ehrhart functions of rational polytopes. \item If $m=n+2$ and $\lambda=(m-1,1)$, then \[ \sum_{k\ge0}s_k^{k\lambda}t^k =\frac{1-t^{m(m-1)}}{\prod_{i=2}^m(1-t^i)}. \] This stretching function is not quasipolynomial on all positive integers and is not even eventually the Ehrhart function of a rational polytope. Hence permanent-side PH1 is false without any encoding restriction. \item If $n=2$, $m\ge5$, and $\lambda=(m-1,1)$, then $s_k^{k\lambda}=\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ for $k\ge1$, whereas $s_0^0=1$. This also cannot be the Ehrhart function of a rational polytope, even if equality is required only for all sufficiently large stretches. \item If $n=2$ and $m=3$, the ray $\lambda=(1,1,1)

label: thm:padding-nonnormal
statement: For every $m>n\ge2$, the cone $Z$ is not normal. Consequently it does not have rational singularities.

label: lem:two-matrix-invariants
statement: If $\ell(\lambda)\le2$, then \[ a_m(\lambda,d) =\bigl[\operatorname{Sym}^{d}(\operatorname{Sym}^{m}\mathbb C^2): S_\lambda\mathbb C^2\bigr]. \]

label: thm:encoding-witness
statement: For every $m\ge3$ and $k\ge0$, \[ a_m\bigl(k(m-1,1),k\bigr) =[z^k]\prod_{i=2}^{m}\frac1{1-z^i}. \] This quasipolynomial has degree $m-2$. Every rational polytope with this Ehrhart quasipolynomial has affine dimension $m-2$. Hence the uniform encoding bound in determinant-side PH1 of GCT VI is false.

label: prop:encoding-witness-replacement
statement: For this ray alone, an exact Ehrhart formula exists with ambient dimension $m-1$ and encoding length $O(m\log m)$.

label: lem:long-row-sharpened
statement: Let $\lambda\vdash md$ occur in $\operatorname{Sym}^{d}(\operatorname{Sym}^{m}\mathbb C^{m^2})$, put $b=|\overline\lambda|$ and $s=\lambda_2$, and suppose $b>0$. If $k=b+s\le d$ and $sk\le m$, then $\lambda$ occurs in $\mathbb C[\mathcal D_m]_d^*$.

label: thm:new-variable-no-occurrence
statement: Let $n\ge2$ and $m>n$. Every representation occurring in the coordinate ring of the new-variable padded permanent orbit closure also occurs, in the same degree, in the coordinate ring of $\mathcal D_m$ if either \[ m\ge(n+1)^{25},\qquad\text{or}\qquad n\ge5\ \text{and}\ m\ge n^{25}. \] Consequently no strong occurrence obstruction exists in either range.

label: prop:robust-contradiction
statement: Assume the counting clauses of PH1 on both sides, even only for all sufficiently large stretches. In either range of Theorem~\ref{thm:new-variable-no-occurrence}, there is no robust obstruction in the sense of GCT VI. Thus OH is incompatible with these counting clauses, irrespective of the encoding length of the polytopes.

label: prop:fixed-ehrhart-failures
statement: The two determinant-side stretching functions \[ A(k)=a_3(k(7,5),4k),\qquad B(k)=a_4(k(11,9),5k) \] are not Ehrhart quasipolynomials of rational polytopes, of any encoding size. The ordinary Kronecker ray \[ C(k)=g((6k,6k),(7k,5k),(6k,4k,2k)) \] has the same failure.

label: prop:central-ehrhart-failures
statement: The determinant-side stretching functions at \[ (m,d,\lambda)=(5,6,(15,15))\quad\hbox{and}\quad (6,7,(21,21)) \] are not Ehrhart quasipolynomials of rational polytopes. In both cases, the coefficient at stretch one is zero and the signed reciprocal evaluation at minus one is one. These witnesses satisfy the padding first-row condition whenever $3\le n<m$.

label: lem:binary-strict-ray-dimension
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $0<b<md/2$, and write $F_{m,d,b}(k)=a_m(k(md-b,b),kd)$. The ray algebra with Hilbert function $F_{m,d,b}$ is a Cohen--Macaulay domain of dimension $m-1$.

label: prop:binary-reciprocity-identity
statement: Suppose $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $0<b\le md/2$. For every integer $k\ge1$: \begin{enumerate} \item If $q>0$, then $\deg F=m-2$ and \begin{equation} (-1)^{m-2}F(-k)=C_m(kd-m-1,kq-2). \end{equation} \item If $q=0$, then $\deg F=m-3$ and \begin{equation} (-1)^{m-3}F(-k)=h_m(kd-m-1). \end{equation} \end{enumerate} Negative evaluations are evaluations of the quasipolynomial constituents. The conventions on negative shifted degrees apply in both identities.

label: prop:binary-reciprocity-no-obstruction
statement: For every $m\ge7$, every $d\ge1$, every integer $0\le2b\le md$, and every $k\ge1$, the determinant-side binary stretching function satisfies \begin{equation} 0\le(-1)^{\deg F}F(-k)\le F(k). \end{equation} Thus the elementary Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity inequality cannot supply an all-large-$m$ binary obstruction, regardless of the chamber, the stretch, or replacement by a Veronese ray.

label: thm:permanent-discriminant
statement: Let $n\ge2$, $m=n+2$, and let $Z$ be the reduced orbit closure of $y^2\operatorname{per}_n$. Put $\lambda=(m-1,1)$, and let $s_k^{k\lambda}$ be its coordinate-ring multiplicity. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{k\ge0}s_k^{k\lambda}t^k =\frac{1-t^{m(m-1)}}{\prod_{i=2}^{m}(1-t^i)}. \end{equation} The function $k\mapsto s_k^{k\lambda}$ is not a quasipolynomial on the positive integers. In particular, it cannot be the Ehrhart function of a rational polytope. Permanent-side PH1 of GCT VI, Hypothesis~7.6.2, is false, even with no bound on the size of a proposed polytope.

label: prop:permanent-exact-correction
title: The exact finite correction
statement: Put \[ A=\frac{(m-1)(m-2)}2,\qquad D=m(m-1),\qquad S=\sum_{i=2}^m i, \] so $D-S=A$. Let $\widehat p_m$ be the global quasipolynomial extending $p_m(k)=[t^k]\prod_{i=2}^m(1-t^i)^{-1}$ from nonnegative integers, and define \[ q_m(k)=\widehat p_m(k)-\widehat p_m(k-D). \] The permanent-side multiplicity $h_m(k)=s_k^{(k(m-1),k)}$ satisfies \[ h_m(k)-q_m(k)= \begin{cases} (-1)^m p_m(A-k),&0\leq k\leq A,\\ 0,&k>A. \end{cases} \] Thus its eventual quasipolynomial begins after $A$, and this cutoff is sharp. The polynomial part of its rational Hilbert series is exactly \[ (-1)^m\sum_{k=0}^A p_m(A-k)t^k. \]

label: cor:permanent-discriminant-no-eventual-ehrhart
statement: For every $m=n+2\ge4$, the square-padding stretching function is not eventually the Ehrhart function of any rational polytope.

label: prop:permanent-inhomogeneous-polytope
statement: The same square-padding multiplicity has the exact positive formula \[ s_k^{k\lambda}= \#\left\{(x_2,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{m-1}: \sum_{i=2}^{m}i x_i=k,\quad x_m\le m-2\right\}. \] The defining inequalities and equation have total binary encoding length $O(m\log m+\log(k+1))$ when the sparse description is used.

label: lem:binary-centered-ray
statement: Let $Y\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}^m\mathbb C^2$ be a reduced closed $\mathrm{GL}_2$-stable cone meeting the open set where the leading coefficient is nonzero. Let $Y^{\mathrm{cen}}$ be its slice of monic forms whose next coefficient is zero, with coefficient $a_j$ assigned weight $j$, for $2\le j\le m$. Then \[ \operatorname{mult}_{(k(m-1),k)}\mathbb C[Y]_k =\dim\mathbb C[Y^{\mathrm{cen}}]_k, \] where the grading on the right is this weighted grading.

label: thm:permanent-large-padding
statement: Let $n=2$ and $m\ge5$, and let $Z$ be the reduced orbit closure of $y^{m-2}\operatorname{per}_2$ with an independent padding variable. For $\lambda=(m-1,1)$, \[ s_k^{k\lambda}=\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2}\right\rfloor\quad(k\ge1), \qquad s_0^0=1. \] Equivalently, \[ \sum_{k\ge0}s_k^{k\lambda}t^k =\frac{1-t+t^3}{(1-t)(1-t^2)}. \] There is no rational polytope whose lattice-point counts at all sufficiently large integral dilations equal this stretching function. The witness has height two and satisfies $\lambda_1\ge m-n$.

label: prop:permanent-minimal-padding
statement: For $n=2$, $m=3$, and $\lambda=(1,1,1)$, the reduced orbit closure of $y\operatorname{per}_2$ satisfies \[ \sum_{k\ge0}s_k^{(k,k,k)}t^k =\frac{1-t^{12}}{(1-t^4)(1-t^6)} =\frac1{1-t^2}-t^2. \] In particular this stretching function is not quasipolynomial on all positive integers and is not an Ehrhart function.

label: cor:permanent-n2-all-padding
statement: For permanent size $n=2$, the permanent-side PH1 counting assertion fails for every determinant size $m>2$, even without an encoding bound. The witnesses have height at most three and satisfy the padding first-row condition.

label: prop:cone-difference-empty
statement: Let $T$ be the additive semigroup of pairs $(d,\lambda)$ with $s_d^\lambda>0$, and let $S$ be the corresponding semigroup with $a_m(\lambda,d)>0$. If $n\ge5,m\ge n^{25}$, or $n\ge2,m\ge(n+1)^{25}$, then \[ T\subseteq S,\qquad \operatorname{cone}(T)\subseteq\operatorname{cone}(S). \] In this range the geometric-obstruction discovery problem formulated by PH1* has the constant answer that its cone difference is empty.

label: prop:general-padding-nonnormal
statement: Let $U$ be a complex vector space, let $0\ne h\in\operatorname{Sym}^eU$ have degree $e\ge2$, and suppose $h$ has no linear factor. Put $W=\mathbb Cy\oplus U$. For every positive integer $r$, the reduced affine orbit closure \[ Z(h,r)=\overline{GL(W)\cdot(y^rh)} \subseteq\operatorname{Sym}^{e+r}W \] is not normal and hence does not have rational singularities.

label: prop:eh-degree-incompatibility
statement: The nonzero homogeneous polynomial $E_{a,b}$ has ordinary degree $ab^a$. For fixed $b$, this degree exceeds every fixed power of the scalar-input count $N$ as $a\to\infty$. In particular, the degree is not $O(N^2)$.

label: thm:eh-terminal-stabilizer
statement: For every $d\ge1$ and $w\ge2$, the full affine stabilizer of the polynomial $H$ in $SL(Y)$ contains a faithful algebraic subgroup isomorphic to $SL_w$. Its action preserves the input/parameter decomposition, every level, and every coefficient-node block individually. It also belongs to the projective line stabilizer and acts trivially on the line $\mathbb C H$.

label: prop:eh-input-fixed-stabilizer
statement: If $d\ge2$, the full affine stabilizer of $H$ in $SL(Y)$ also contains a faithful copy of $SL_w$ fixing every input variable pointwise and preserving all levels.

label: cor:eh-stabilizer-incompatibility
statement: For $w\ge2$, the full stabilizer of the literal universal form \eqref{eq:eh-recursion} in $GL(Y)$ or $SL(Y)$ is not a finite extension of an algebraic torus.

label: thm:relaxed-torus-hardness
statement: Fix any polynomial threshold $q$. The following promised nonvanishing problem is NP-complete: the input is a faithful polynomial embedding of an algebraic torus $T$ into $GL(V)$, a torus character $\pi$, and an integer $A>q(\operatorname{rank}(x))$; decide whether $A\pi$ occurs in $\operatorname{Sym}^{A}V$. Here the outer weight before stretching is $(1)$, and $\operatorname{rank}(x)$ is the parameter of GCT VI, \S3.4. In particular, the polynomial-time rank-relaxed subgroup decision assertion of Theorem~3.3.6(a), if asserted without its sufficient positivity assumptions, implies $P=NP$.

label: thm:main-indices
statement: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For every $n\ge4$, $H_n$ has a simple pole at every primitive $2^{n-1}$th root of unity. Every positive rational form for $H_n$ has a denominator weight at least $2^{n-1}$; the same lower bound holds for the degree of some member of every homogeneous system of parameters of its canonical ring. \item For every $c<1/4$, all sufficiently large $n$ satisfy \[ p(f_n)>2^{cn},\qquad s(f_n)\ge2^{cn}. \] One may take the explicit bounds $p(f_n)>2^{n/8}$ and $s(f_n)\ge2^{n/8}$ for $n\ge192$. At $n=9$, one has $p(f_9)>7$ and $s(f_9)\ge7$. \item For every $n\ge2$, there is an integer $r\ge0$ such that $K_n$ has a pole at every primitive root of order $2^{n-1}3^r$. Every quasiperiod is divisible by that order. Every eventual linear recurrence with constant coefficients has order at least $2^{n-2}+1$. For $2\le n\le5$ the choice $r=0$ is valid; in particular $K_5$ has a pole at every primitive sixteenth root. \item Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $\lambda\vdash md$ have at most $h$ rows, with $2\le h\le m^2$. For the full determinant stabilizer, including transposition, put $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$. Then \[ s(F)\le p(F)<(2mh)^{72h^3-9h+17}<m^{288h^3}. \] Thus every fixed height has a polynomial strict-index bound in $m$, uniformly in $d$ and $\lambda$. The one-row indices are zero. For $\lambda=(md-b,b)$ with $0\le2b\le md$, a sharper bound holds. For the full determinant stabilizer, including transposition, let $a(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$. Its ray algebra h

label: thm:main-vertex-bound
statement: Let $R$ be a finitely generated positively graded Cohen--Macaulay domain over $\mathbb C$, with $R_0=\mathbb C$, dimension $n\ge1$, and $a(R)<0$. If homogeneous elements of degrees at most $S$ have common zero set equal to the vertex of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, then $F(k)=\dim_{\mathbb C}R_k$ is a quasipolynomial for every nonnegative integer and \[ s(F)\le p(F)\le202n^4S^6. \] The same bound holds for every Veronese function $F(ak)$.

label: prop:cubic-parameter-degree
statement: Every homogeneous system of parameters of $T_n$ contains an element of degree at least $2^{n-1}$. The associated ordinary plethysm input has inner shape $(3)$, outer shape $(n/g)$, and output shape $((3/g)^n)$. Its parameter in GCT VI, Hypothesis 1.6.7, is $\binom{n+2}{3}^2+n+1$.

label: thm:extremal-cubic-support
statement: Suppose the support matrix of a cubic in $n\ge2$ variables has $\mathbf1$ in its rational column span. If a diagonal matrix $A$ of finite power-of-two order fixes the cubic, then $\operatorname{ord}(\det A)\le2^{n-1}$. Equality holds only when, after permutation of the variables, the support is precisely \eqref{eq:chain-cubic}. In that case diagonal rescaling makes all coefficients one, and $A$ itself has order $2^{n-1}$.

label: lem:unique-fixed-component
statement:
Let $R$ be a finitely generated positively graded complex domain with $R_0=\mathbb C$, and let $u$ multiply $R_d$ by $\zeta^d$, where $\zeta$ is primitive of order $M$. Suppose the fixed scheme in $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ has a unique component $Y$ of maximal dimension $\delta\ge1$ and that $X$ is smooth at its generic point. Let $
u_1,\ldots,
u_c$ be the conormal eigenvalues there. Set \[ e_Y=\lim_{z	o1}(1-z)^\delta \sum_{j\ge0}\dim\mathbb C[Y]_{Mj}z^j. \] Then $e_Y>0$, every $
