label: lem:chain-stabilizer
statement: For $n\ge4$, the projective automorphism group of $F_n$ is cyclic of order $M$. Its exact $SL_n$ stabilizer is the scalar group $\mu_g$, which acts trivially on cubic forms. At its quotient point $p_n\in X_n=\operatorname{Spec}T_n$, $X_n$ is smooth, and the $\mu_M$ fixed scheme is smooth of dimension one.

label: thm:cubic-poles
statement: For $n\ge4$, the support of the grading fixed scheme $X_n^{\mu_M}$ is the closure $Y_n$ of the grading orbit of $p_n$. Away from the origin this is a smooth curve in the smooth locus of $X_n$. The Hilbert series $H_n(t)=\sum_{s\ge0}f_n(s)t^s$ has a simple pole at every primitive $M$th root $\zeta$, with \[ C_n(\zeta):=\lim_{t\to\zeta}(1-t^M)H_n(t) =\det(1-\zeta\mid N^*_{Y_n/X_n})^{-1}\ne0. \] No root supporting a Hilbert pole has multiplicative order with two-part greater than $M$, and among orders with two-part $M$ only the order $M$ occurs.

label: prop:positive-normal-weights
statement: For a primitive $M$th root $\zeta$, \[ C_n(\zeta)=\prod_{b\in\mathcal S_n}(1-\zeta^{gb})^{-1}, \qquad |\mathcal S_n|=\binom n3. \] This identity includes the complex phase of the residue.

label: prop:paired-constituents
statement: One has $v_2(L)=n-1$ and, as polynomial identities in $X$, \[ q_a(X)-q_{a+L/2}(X)=2W_n(a). \] Consequently, if an integer $x\ge0$ satisfies $2W_n(x)>f_n(x)$, then $p(f_n)>x$ and $s(f_n)\ge x$.

label: lem:cubic-complex-recursion
statement: For $n\ge6$ and every primitive $M_n$th root $\eta$, \begin{equation} c_n(\eta)=\frac14c_{n-1}(\eta^2)B_{n-2}(\eta). \end{equation} This is an identity of complex numbers, including their phases.

label: lem:cubic-effective-energy
statement: Let $k\ge4$, $q=2^{k+1}$, and let $a$ be odd modulo $q$. Put \[ u_i=e^{2\pi i a(-2)^i/q}\quad(0\le i<k),\qquad \phi(\theta)=-\log|\cos(\theta/2)|, \] and \[ \mathcal E_k(a)= \sum_{(i,j,\ell)\text{ retained}} \phi(\arg(u_i u_j u_\ell)) =-\log\frac{|B_k(e^{2\pi ia/q})|}{2^{t_k}}. \] Write $\mathcal E_k^*$ for the energy at either distinguished exponent. For every $k\ge4$, \begin{equation} \mathcal E_k^*\le\frac{k^2}{32},\qquad \mathcal E_k(a)\ge \frac{k^2}{8}-\frac{9k}{8}+\frac23 \quad(a\text{ nondistinguished}). \end{equation} In particular, with \[ \gamma(k)=\frac{3k^2}{32}-\frac{9k}{8}+\frac23, \] one has \begin{equation} \frac{|B_k(e^{2\pi ia/q})|}{|B_k(\eta_{k+2})|} \le e^{-\gamma(k)} \quad(a\text{ nondistinguished}). \end{equation} Moreover $\gamma(k)>0$ for $k\ge12$.

label: lem:cubic-residue-dominance-512
statement: For every $n\ge192$, \begin{equation} R_n:= \sum_{\substack{\eta\text{ primitive }M_n\text{th}\\ \eta\ne\eta_n,\overline\eta_n}} \frac{|c_n(\eta)|}{A_n}<\frac18. \end{equation} For every $n\ge6$, \begin{equation} \log_2 A_n> \frac{n^4}{24}-\frac{83n^3}{192} +\frac{23n^2}{24}-\frac{19n}{12}-14. \end{equation} In particular $A_n>2^{n^4/26}$ for every $n\ge135$.

label: thm:cubic-exponential-indices
statement: For every real $c<1/4$ and all sufficiently large $n$, \[ p(f_n)>2^{cn},\qquad s(f_n)\ge2^{cn}. \] In particular these inequalities hold with $c=1/8$ for every $n\ge192$. Thus PH2 and SH(a) for ordinary plethysm, GCT VI Hypotheses 1.6.6 and 1.6.5(a), fail with fixed inner shape $(3)$.

label: prop:nine-variable-witness
statement: For the cubic plethysm ray, $p(f_9)>7$ and $s(f_9)\ge7$. Moreover the strict-index obstruction can occur at a positive coefficient: $f_9(6)=1$ and $2W_9(6)>1$.

label: prop:kr-cyclic-trace
title: Cyclic trace identity
statement: Let $\tau$ cyclically permute the three tensor factors. Then, for all $n\geq2$ and $s\geq0$, \[ \operatorname{tr}(\tau\mid (R_n)_s)=b_n(s), \qquad k_n(s)-b_n(s)\in3\mathbb Z_{\geq0}. \] In particular $K_n(t)\equiv B_n(t)\pmod3$ coefficient by coefficient.

label: lem:kr-lie-stabilizer
statement: The $\mathfrak{gl}(W)$ stabilizer of $z_n$ is zero for every $n\geq2$.

label: prop:kr-hook-orbit
statement: The $SL(W)$ orbit of $z_n$ is closed. Its full $GL(W)$ stabilizer is cyclic of order $M$, and determinant is faithful on it. The nonzero fixed locus of $\mu_M$ on $U_n/\!/SL(W)$ consists of one grading orbit, and the quotient is smooth along that orbit. The closure of the orbit has density one when its grading is divided by $M$.

label: thm:kr-hook-pole
title: The auxiliary pole
statement: For each primitive $M$th root $\xi$, the series $B_n(t)$ has a simple pole and \[ C_n(\xi)=\lim_{t\to\xi}(1-t^M)B_n(t) \in\mathbb Z[\xi,1/2]^\times. \] If $d\ne M$ has two-primary part at least $M$, then $B_n$ is regular at every primitive $d$th root of unity.

label: lem:kr-isolated-fixed
statement: Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\geq0}A_j$ be a finitely generated graded $\mathbb C$-algebra, with $A_0=\mathbb C$ and finite-dimensional pieces. If the fixed scheme of $\mu_d$ is supported at the origin, then its Hilbert series is regular at every primitive $d$th root.

label: lem:kr-cyclotomic-reduction
title: Cyclotomic reduction
statement: For a prime $p$, write $d=p^r e$ with $p\nmid e$. Then \[ \overline{\Phi_d}(t)= \begin{cases} \overline{\Phi_e}(t),&r=0,\\ \overline{\Phi_e}(t)^{p^{r-1}(p-1)},&r\geq1 \end{cases} \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_p[t]. \] The roots of $\overline{\Phi_e}$ are simple and have exact order $e$.

label: prop:kr-modular-transfer
title: Transfer of a pole through a congruence
statement: Suppose $F,G\in\mathbb Q(t)\cap\mathbb Z[[t]]$ have all finite poles at roots of unity and $F\equiv G\pmod p$ coefficient by coefficient. Let $p\nmid M$. Suppose $G$ has a pole of order $\delta$ at a primitive $M$th root $\zeta$, has no pole at any primitive $Mp^r$th root for $r>0$, and \[ \lim_{t\to\zeta}(1-t^M)^\delta G(t) \] is a unit in the local ring of $\mathbb Z[\zeta]$ at some prime over $p$. Then $F$ has a pole at every primitive $Mp^r$th root for some $r\geq0$.

label: thm:kr-poles
title: Exponential orders of Kronecker pole roots
statement: For every $n\geq2$, there is $r\geq0$ such that $K_n(t)$ has a pole at every primitive $2^{n-1}3^r$th root of unity. Every denominator expression \[ K_n(t)=\frac{P(t)}{\prod_i(1-t^{a_i})^{c_i}},\qquad P\in\mathbb Q[t],\quad a_i,c_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}, \] has some $a_i\geq2^{n-1}$. Every quasi-period of $k_n$ is divisible by $2^{n-1}3^r$. Every constant-coefficient linear recurrence satisfied eventually by $k_n$ has order at least $2^{n-2}+1$.

label: lem:kbg-incidence-determinants
statement: Partition $3n$ rows into three blocks of size $n$. Let $A$ be a $3n\times N$ matrix of linearly independent columns, each of which has one entry equal to $1$ in each block and all other entries zero. Let $D$ be the determinant obtained by deleting one row from each of two different blocks. Then $D\ne0$, and \[ |D|\le B_n. \] More precisely, if $d_{a,i}$ is the number of columns incident with row $i$ of block $a$, then \begin{equation} D^2\le\frac{1}{N^2} \prod_{a=1}^3\prod_{i=1}^n d_{a,i}. \end{equation}

label: lem:kbg-grading-stabilizers
statement: If a root of unity $z$ of order $d$ fixes a nonvertex point of $X_n$ under the normalized grading action, then \[ d\le\lfloor B_n\rfloor. \] This holds without any assumption that the tensor support has full rank or that its stabilizer is finite.

label: lem:kbg-fixed-point-pole-exclusion
statement: Let $R$ be a finitely generated nonnegatively graded complex algebra with $R_0=\C$, and let $z$ have finite order $d$. If $z$ fixes no nonvertex point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ under the grading action, then the Hilbert series of $R$ is regular at $z$.

label: prop:kronecker-pole-order-upper
statement: For every $n\ge2$, every root of unity supporting a pole of $K_n$ has multiplicative order at most \[ \left\lfloor\frac{8\,3^{(3n-6)/2}}{3n-2}\right\rfloor. \] Consequently the exponent in Theorem~\ref{thm:kr-poles} can be chosen with \begin{equation} 0\le r\le \left\lfloor \frac{3n-6}{2}+\log_3\!\left(\frac{8}{3n-2}\right) -(n-1)\log_3 2 \right\rfloor. \end{equation}

label: cor:kbg-pure-eighth-root
statement: The rectangular Kronecker series $K_4$ has an actual pole at every primitive eighth root of unity. In particular, the pure dyadic choice $r=0$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:kr-poles} holds for $n=2,3,4$.

label: lem:kronecker-centered-correlations
statement: In the notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:kbg-incidence-determinants}, put $N=3n-2$ and let $B_a$ be the $n$ by $N$ row block of the incidence matrix, for $a=1,2,3$. There is a positive definite matrix $C$ of size $N-1$, with three identity diagonal blocks of size $n-1$, such that \begin{equation} D^2=\frac{\prod_{a=1}^3\prod_{i=1}^n d_{a,i}}{N^2}\det C. \end{equation} Its eigenvalues lie in $(0,3]$ and its trace is $N-1$. For $a\ne b$, its off-diagonal block satisfies \begin{equation} \|C_{ab}\|_F^2 =\sum_{i,j}\frac{(B_aB_b^{\mathsf T})_{ij}^2} {d_{a,i}d_{b,j}}-1. \end{equation}

label: lem:kronecker-five-incidence-bound
statement: An independent $15$ by $13$ tensor incidence matrix whose every row has degree at least two has $|D|<48$.

label: thm:kronecker-five-pure-dyadic
statement: Every finite-order grading automorphism fixing a nonvertex point of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[(\mathbb C^5)^{\otimes3}]^{\mathrm{SL}_5^3}$, with ordinary degree divided by five, has order at most $47$. Every pole root of $K_5$ has order at most $47$. Consequently $K_5$ has a pole at every primitive sixteenth root, and the choice $r=0$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:kr-poles} is valid for every $2\le n\le5$.

label: prop:printed-positive-form-failure
statement: For $\phi(s)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_{GL_2} (S_{(7s,5s)}\mathbb C^2,\operatorname{Sym}^{4s} (\operatorname{Sym}^3\mathbb C^2))$, one has \[ \phi(s)=\frac{s+r_s}{3},\qquad (r_0,r_1,r_2,r_3,r_4,r_5)=(3,-1,1,0,2,-2), \] \[ \sum_{s\ge0}\phi(s)t^s=\frac{1+t^4}{(1-t^2)(1-t^3)}. \] Thus Theorem 1.6.1(d) of GCT VI is false as printed. The usual Cohen--Macaulay positive form remains valid, and $p(\phi)=s(\phi)=2$.

label: thm:positive-form-index-bound
statement: Suppose a nonzero global quasipolynomial $f$ has generating function \[ F(t)=\frac{H(t)}{\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{a_i})},\qquad H\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}[t]\setminus\{0\},\quad a_i>0. \] Put $A=\max_i a_i$ and $h=\deg H$. Then \[ s(f)\le p(f)\le h+128r^3A^3<rA+128r^3A^3. \] For a nonzero subgroup-restriction ray $f(s)=\dim\operatorname{Hom}_H(V_{s\pi},V_{s\lambda}|_H)$, with connected reductive groups, one has $r\le1+\#\{\alpha\in\Phi_G^+:\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle>0\} \le1+\dim G$. Consequently the proposed PH3 bound would imply PH2 in its stated plethysm parameter. For classical subgroup restrictions the same implication uses $r\le1+(\operatorname{rank}G)^2$.

label: prop:torus-index-families
statement: In the full subgroup-restriction problem, the modular index is unbounded when the source rank parameter is five, and both strict indices are unbounded when it is six. More precisely: \begin{enumerate} \item For $N\ge2$, the embedding $t\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(t^{N+1},t)$ into $GL_2$, with outer weight $(1)$ and torus target weight two, gives stretching function $\mathbf1_{N\mid s}$ and minimum modular index $N$. \item For odd $N\ge3$, the embedding $t\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(t,t^3,t^{N+1})$ into $GL_3$, with the same outer and target weights, gives \[ g_N(s)=\#\{(v,w)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2:2v+Nw=s\}, \qquad p(g_N)=s(g_N)=N-2. \] \end{enumerate} These refute the full subgroup-restriction bounds PH3, PH2, and SH(a), respectively. They have rational-polytope models of constant ambient dimension and description length $O(\log N)$.

label: lem:two-matrix-invariants
statement: For two-row shapes the determinant multiplicity equals $a_m(d,b)$.

label: prop:binary-edge-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $\lambda=(md-b,b)$ with $0\le b\le d$. For the full determinant line-stabilizer ray $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$ one has $F\equiv1$ if $b=0$. If $b\ge1$, then \[ s(F)\le p(F)\le \left\lceil\frac{128(m-1)^3m^3}{b}\right\rceil. \] In particular both strict indices are bounded polynomially in $m$ throughout this range, uniformly in $d$.

label: lem:primitive-zero-sum
statement: Let $w_1,\ldots,w_N$ be integers in $[-Q,P]$, with $P,Q$ positive integers. A nonzero vector $\alpha\in\mathbb N^N$ with $\sum_i\alpha_iw_i=0$ that is minimal under coordinatewise comparison has $\sum_i\alpha_i\le P+Q$, unless it consists of one zero weight, in which case its length is one.

label: lem:bigraded-ray-generators
statement: Let $R=\bigoplus_{a,b\ge0}R_{a,b}$ be a finitely generated bigraded $\mathbb C$-algebra with $R_{0,0}=\mathbb C$ and $R_{0,b}=0$ for $b>0$. Suppose it has bihomogeneous generators of bidegrees $(a_i,b_i)$ with $1\le a_i\le A$ and $0\le b_i\le B$. For positive $d$ and nonnegative $r$ with $r/d\le m$, the ray algebra \[ R(d,r)=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}R_{kd,kr}, \] graded by $k$, is generated in degrees at most \[ M=\max\{A,A(mA+B)\}. \]

label: thm:binary-ray-bounds
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $\lambda=(md-b,b)$ with $0\le2b\le md$. Put \[ F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda},\quad D=\frac32(m+3)m^6,\quad M=(m+1)D^2\le18m^{15}. \] Then the graded algebra with Hilbert function $F$ is generated in degrees at most $M$. If some $F(k)$ with $k>0$ is nonzero, let $g$ be the greatest common divisor of all such $k$. Then \[ k\ge M^2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \bigl(F(k)>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ g\mid k\bigr). \] The ray algebra is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain with negative $a$-invariant. In particular $F$ is quasipolynomial for every $k\ge0$, not only eventually. A sharper, quadratic-degree denominator bound is given in Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-universal-denominator} below.

label: thm:binary-universal-denominator
title: A common denominator for all two-row rays
statement: For every $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $\lambda=(md-b,b)$ with $0\le2b\le md$, put $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$ and \[ D_m(t)=\prod_{i=2}^m(1-t^i),\qquad L_m=\deg D_m=\frac{m(m+1)}2-1. \] Then \[ \sum_{k\ge0}F(k)t^k=\frac{N_{m,d,b}(t)}{D_m(t)}, \qquad N_{m,d,b}(t)\in\mathbb Z[t],\quad \deg N_{m,d,b}<L_m. \] No assertion of coefficientwise nonnegativity of $N_{m,d,b}$ is made. Every pole has root order at most $m$; at a primitive $q$th root with $q\ge2$ its multiplicity is at most $\lfloor m/q\rfloor$, and at one it is at most $m-1$. Thus $F$ has a constant-coefficient linear recurrence of order at most $L_m=O(m^2)$, valid for all indices at least $L_m$, and its minimal quasiperiod divides $\operatorname{lcm}(2,\ldots,m)$. Here ``common'' refers to the displayed Hilbert series as $d$ and $b$ vary. Theorem~\ref{thm:binary-universal-module-denominator} below strengthens this to the Hilbert series of all finite graded modules, giving a universal denominator in Derksen's sense.

label: lem:binary-strict-ray-dimension
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $0<b<md/2$, and write $F_{m,d,b}(k)=m^{kd}_{k(md-b,b)}$. The ray algebra with Hilbert function $F_{m,d,b}$ is a Cohen--Macaulay domain of dimension $m-1$. In particular, the leading nonzero coefficient of $N_{m,d,b}$ is positive.

label: thm:binary-small-degree-indices
statement: Let $m\in\{3,4\}$, $d\ge1$, and $0\le b\le md/2$ be integers, and put \[ F(k)=a_m(kd,kb)=m^{kd}_{(k(md-b),kb)}. \] Then $s(F)\le p(F)\le2$. The bound on $p$ is sharp for both binary degrees. More precisely, for $(m,d,b)=(3,4,5)$ one has $p(F)=s(F)=2$, while for $(m,d,b)=(4,2,3)$ one has $p(F)=2$ and $s(F)=1$.

label: thm:binary-first-chamber-positive
statement: Let $m\ge5$, $d\ge1$, and $d<b\le2d$. Then \[ N_{m,d,b}(t)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}[t]. \] Consequently the strict positivity and saturation indices satisfy \[ s(F_{m,d,b})\le p(F_{m,d,b}) \le L_m-1+128(m-1)^3m^3<129m^6. \] Together with the edge range $0\le b\le d$, this gives a bound polynomial in $m$, independent of $d$ and $b$, for all two-row rays with $0\le b\le2d$ and $m\ge5$.

label: lem:binary-subset-box-monotonicity
statement: For every $m\ge3$, the subset sums of $\{2,\ldots,m\}$ are exactly \[ \{0\}\ \cup\ \{2,3,\ldots,L_m-2\}\ \cup\ \{L_m\}. \] For $b\ge1$ put \[ B_b(t)= \sum_{\substack{0\le u_i<b\ (2\le i\le m)\\ b\mid\sum_{i=2}^m i u_i}} t^{\sum_{i=2}^m i u_i/b}. \] Then, for every $2\le k\le L_m-2$, \[ [t^k]B_{b+1}(t)\ge[t^k]B_b(t). \] No monotonicity assertion is made for $k=1$ or $k=L_m-1$.

label: cor:binary-n2-padding-indices
statement: Suppose $n=2$, $m\ge5$, and $\lambda=(md-b,b)$ satisfies the first-row condition $\lambda_1\ge(m-n)d$ required for occurrence on the new-variable padded-permanent side. Then the determinant ray $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$ has \[ s(F)\le p(F)<129m^6. \]

label: lem:universal-denominator-normalization
statement: Let $A$ be a positively graded finite-type complex algebra with $A_0=\mathbb C$ and $\dim A=\ell\ge1$. Suppose $A$ is generated by homogeneous elements of degrees at most the integer $M\ge1$. Suppose further that positive integers $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_\ell$ satisfy \[ U_A(t)\ \mid\ \prod_{i=1}^{\ell}(1-t^{\beta_i}). \] Set \[ E_i=\beta_i\left\lceil\frac{M^2}{\beta_i}\right\rceil. \] Then $A$ has a homogeneous system of parameters with degrees $E_1,\ldots,E_\ell$. In particular their maximum is less than $M^2+\max_i\beta_i$. More generally, any prescribed degrees $E_1,\ldots,E_\ell\ge M^2$ for which $U_A$ divides $\prod_i(1-t^{E_i})$ are the degrees of a homogeneous system of parameters.

label: lem:affine-partition-denominator
statement: Let \[ P_m(n)=[z^n]\prod_{i=2}^m(1-z^i)^{-1},\qquad P_m(n)=0\quad(n<0),\qquad m\ge3. \] For all integers $c,s$, the generating function $\sum_{k\ge0}P_m(ck+s)t^k$ has reduced denominator dividing $D_m(t)=\prod_{i=2}^m(1-t^i)$. The same conclusion holds after changing finitely many terms of the sequence, or summing finitely many such sequences.

label: thm:binary-universal-module-denominator
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, $0\le2b\le md$, and $r=md-2b$. Let \[ A_{m,d,b}=\bigoplus_{k\ge0} \left(\mathbb C[ \operatorname{Sym}^m\mathbb C^2\oplus\mathbb C^2] ^{\mathrm{SL}_2}\right)_{kd,kr} \] with its ray grading $k$. Then \[ U_{A_{m,d,b}}(t)\mid D_m(t)=\prod_{i=2}^m(1-t^i). \] This assertion includes the central case $r=0$; it is stronger than the common denominator assertion for the rings' own Hilbert series.

label: thm:all-binary-strict-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $\lambda=(md-b,b)$ with $0\le2b\le md$. Put \[ F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda},\qquad M=18m^{15},\qquad H=M^2+m=324m^{30}+m. \] Then the determinant ray algebra has a homogeneous system of parameters of degrees less than $H$, except that the constant Hilbert-function case $b=0$ is simply $\mathbb C[u]$ with $\deg u=1$. In every case its strict indices satisfy \[ s(F)\le p(F) \le mH+128m^3H^3 <5\cdot10^9m^{93}. \] In particular SH(a) and PH2 hold uniformly for determinant-side partitions of height at most two when polynomial dependence on the natural parameter $m$ is allowed.

label: cor:large-binary-parameter-degrees
statement: Let $m\ge3$ and let $e_1,\ldots,e_{m-2}$ be integers at least $9m^{14}$. Suppose they satisfy these conditions: \begin{itemize} \item if $m$ is odd, all $e_i$ are even, and for each integer $t>1$ at least $\lfloor(m-1)/t\rfloor$ of them are divisible by $2t$; \item if $m$ is even, for each integer $t>1$ at least $\lfloor(m-1)/t\rfloor$ are divisible by $t$; if in addition $m\equiv2\pmod4$, at least $m/2$ of them are even. \end{itemize} Then $\mathbb C[\operatorname{Sym}^m\mathbb C^2]^{\mathrm{SL}_2}$ has a homogeneous system of parameters of degrees $e_1,\ldots,e_{m-2}$.

label: prop:binary-positive-numerator-implication
title: Conditional polynomial bound
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $0<b<md/2$. If $N_{m,d,b}(t)$ has nonnegative coefficients, then \[ s(F)\le p(F)\le R_m-1+128(m-1)^3m^3 <129m^6. \] Thus nonnegativity of these numerators for all strict-interior two-row rays would improve the uniform bound to a polynomial of degree six, independent of $d$ and $b$.

label: thm:symmetric-adjoint-stability
statement: Suppose $m\ge2$, $d\ge b=|\rho|$, and $\lambda=(md-b,\rho)$. Then the determinant-stabilizer multiplicity is \[ m^d_\lambda =\dim\mathcal A_{m,h}[\rho]^{\tau} =\dim\left(S_\rho\mathfrak{sl}_m\right) ^{\mathrm{GL}_m\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle}. \] More precisely, the highest-weight spaces on the two sides are identified by an explicit transposition-equivariant map. Applying this map at every stretch $k$ identifies their graded multiplicity algebras, not only their graded dimensions.

label: cor:rectangular-tail-reduction
statement: Let $h,a\ge1$, let $d\ge ah$, and let $\lambda=(md-ah,a^h)$. Then \[ \sum_{k\ge0}m^{kd}_{k\lambda}t^k =\sum_{k\ge0}\dim \left(\mathbb C[(\mathfrak{sl}_m)^h]^{ \mathrm{GL}_m\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle \,\times\,\mathrm{SL}_h}\right)_{ahk}t^k. \] The subscript on the right is ordinary polynomial degree in the matrix entries. When $h\le n^2$ the determinant partitions have height at most $n^2+1$, as required in the determinant-side hypotheses.

label: tailpole:thm:root-orders
statement: Every nonvertex point of $\Spec\mathcal A_{m,\rho}$ has grading stabilizer of order at most $B(m,h)$. For $\Spec\mathcal A_{m,\rho}^+$, the bound is $2B(m,h)$. The corresponding Hilbert series are therefore regular at roots of unity of order greater than these bounds. In particular, \[ B(m,1)=m,\qquad B(m,2)=\left\lfloor\frac{(m+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor \quad(m\geq3),\qquad B(m,h)\leq2^{m-1}. \] For each fixed $h$, the stabilizer bound has the sharp asymptotic form \[ B(m,h)=(1+o(1))(m/h)^h \qquad(m\longrightarrow\infty). \]

label: tailpole:lem:incidence-minors
title: Colored incidence minors
statement: Let a directed graph on at most $m$ vertices have edges colored by $1,\ldots,h$, with loops and parallel edges allowed. Let $D$ be a full-row-rank reduced incidence matrix of the graph, obtained by removing one vertex row in each connected component, and let $C$ be its color matrix: each column of $C$ is the coordinate vector of its edge color. Put \[ M=\begin{pmatrix}D\\C\end{pmatrix}, \qquad q_0=\operatorname{rank}D,\qquad r=\operatorname{rank}M-q_0. \] If $r>0$, there is a nonsingular square minor of $M$ of full rank, with determinant $\Delta$, such that \[ 0<|\Delta|\leq B(m,h). \] More precisely, every full-rank minor using all $q_0$ incidence rows and any $r$ color rows satisfies \[ |\Delta| \leq \max_{\substack{e_1,\ldots,e_r\geq1\\ e_1+\cdots+e_r\leq q_0+r}} e_1\cdots e_r. \]

label: tailpole:cor:stable-determinant
statement: Let $\rho$ be a partition of height $h$ and let $d\geq|\rho|$. For $\lambda=(md-|\rho|,\rho)$, the stable determinant stretching series \[ \sum_{k\geq0}m^{kd}_{k\lambda}t^k \] has no pole at a root of unity of order greater than $2B(m,h)$.

label: heightthree:thm:parameters
title: Fixed loci and parameter degrees
statement: The variety $X_m$ has dimension $D_m=m^2-4$. If $3\leq e\leq m$ and $\zeta$ is a primitive $e$th root of unity, then \begin{equation} \dim X_m^\zeta\ \geq\ \left\lfloor\frac{(m-e+2)^2}{4}\right\rfloor+m-2. \end{equation} If $f_1,\ldots,f_{D_m}$ is any homogeneous system of parameters of $R_m^+$, with normalized degrees $d_1,\ldots,d_{D_m}$, then \begin{equation} D_m\log\max_i d_i \ \geq\ \sum_{\substack{3\leq p\leq m\\p\ {\rm prime}}} \left(\left\lfloor\frac{(m-p+2)^2}{4}\right\rfloor+m-2\right) \log p. \end{equation} In particular, uniformly over all such systems of parameters, \begin{equation} \log\max_i d_i\ \geq\ \left(\frac1{12}+o(1)\right)m \qquad(m\longrightarrow\infty). \end{equation} Thus, for every $c<1/12$ and all sufficiently large $m$, every homogeneous system of parameters contains an element of normalized degree at least $e^{cm}$.

label: heightthree:lem:binomial-closed
statement: If $e\geq3$ and $cd\ne0$, the binary form $cx^e+dy^e$ has finite $\SL_2$ stabilizer and closed affine $\SL_2$ orbit.

label: heightthree:lem:irreducible-trace-fiber
statement: If $(A,B)$ generates $\Mat_m$, its simultaneous-conjugation quotient fiber is a single orbit, which is closed.

label: heightthree:lem:full-orbit-closed
statement: Every pair in $U_N$ has a closed orbit under $G_m\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle$ and finite effective stabilizer. Moreover, $\dim X_m=m^2-4$.

label: heightthree:prop:cyclic-image-dimension
statement: The image of $U_N$ in $X_m$ has dimension \begin{equation} \sum_iN_iN_{i+1}-1. \end{equation}

label: thm:height-three-polynomial-generators
statement: For $m\ge3$, the nullcone of the full group defining $A_m$ is cut out by invariants of ordinary degree at most $4m^8$. The algebra $A_m$ is generated in normalized degrees at most \begin{equation} 3(m^2-4)m^{16}<3m^{18}. \end{equation}

label: graphprime:thm:fixed-bound
statement: There are absolute constants $C$ and $p_0$ with the following property. If $p\geq p_0$ is prime, $m\leq p$, and $\zeta$ is a primitive $p$th root of unity, then \begin{equation} \dim X_m^\zeta\geq \bigl(m-2\sqrt p-Cp^{1/4}-C\bigr)_+, \qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}. \end{equation} More precisely, put \begin{equation} n=\lceil\sqrt p\rceil,\qquad j=\lfloor\sqrt{n^2-p}\rfloor,\qquad r=n-j,\quad s=n+j,\quad v=rs-p. \end{equation} Whenever $r+s+v\leq m\leq p$, one has \begin{equation} \dim X_m^\zeta\geq m-r-s-v+1. \end{equation}

label: graphprime:lem:diamond-enlargement
statement: For every integer $m$ with $N_0\leq m\leq p$, there is a strongly connected colored subgraph $\Gamma$ of this cyclic graph, containing $\Gamma_0$, with exactly $m$ vertices and $E$ edges, such that \begin{equation} E-m\geq m-N_0+1. \end{equation} The graph may be taken to contain every allowed colored edge between its vertices.

label: graphprime:lem:closed-orbits
statement: Every pair in $U$ has a closed, nonzero orbit under $G_m=\PGL_m\times\SL_2$.

label: graphprime:lem:image-dimension
statement: The closure of the image of $F$ in $(\slm)^2/\!/G_m$ has dimension at least $E-m$.

label: graphprime:thm:one-sixth
statement: Let $d_1,\ldots,d_{D_m}$ be the normalized degrees of any homogeneous system of parameters of $R_m^+$, where $D_m=m^2-4$. Uniformly over all such systems, \begin{equation} \log\max_i d_i\geq\left(\frac16+o(1)\right)m \qquad(m\longrightarrow\infty). \end{equation} In particular, for every $c<1/6$ and all sufficiently large $m$, every homogeneous system of parameters contains an element of normalized degree at least $\exp(cm)$.

label: prop:adjoint-pair-parity-elements
statement: For every $m\ge4$, there are nonzero elements \[ D_m\in B_{m,2}^{+},\qquad T_m\in B_{m,3}^{-},\qquad U_m\in B_{m,6}^{-},\qquad J_m\in B_{m,9}^{+}. \] Consequently \[ B_{m,a}^{+}\ne0\quad(a\ge8),\qquad B_{m,a}^{-}\ne0\quad(a\ge5). \] The elements $D_m,T_m$ are nonzero already for $m=3$. In particular, transpose is not the scalar $(-1)^a$ on every Pl\"ucker-degree-$a$ space.

label: thm:adjoint-pair-canonical-module
statement: For every $m\ge3$, the ring $A_m$ is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain of dimension $m^2-4$, and its graded canonical module satisfies \begin{equation} (\omega_{A_m})_a\cong B_{m,a-r}^{\eta_m}. \end{equation} A sector with negative degree is interpreted as zero. In particular, if $f_m(a)=\dim (A_m)_a$, its Hilbert function is a quasipolynomial already for all $a\ge0$, and \begin{equation} (-1)^{m^2-5}f_m(-a) =\dim B_{m,a-r}^{\eta_m}\qquad(a\ge1). \end{equation}

label: cor:adjoint-pair-reciprocity-barrier
statement: Let $m\ge4$ and $a\ge1$, and put \[ F_a(k)=\dim B_{m,ak}^{+}. \] Then $\deg F_a=m^2-5$ and, for every integer $k\ge1$, \begin{equation} 0\le(-1)^{m^2-5}F_a(-k)\le F_a(k). \end{equation} Consequently no stable determinant ray $\lambda=(md-2a,a,a)$ with $d\ge2a$ and $m\ge4$ violates the elementary Ehrhart--Macdonald reciprocity inequality.

label: cor:stable-m3-rectangular-reciprocity
statement: The full-transpose stable rectangular two-row adjoint tails also pass elementary reciprocity for $m=3$ and every Veronese.

label: thm:arbitrary-two-row-tail-canonical
statement: Suppose $m\ge3$ and $\alpha>\beta>0$. Set $N=\alpha+\beta$, $q=\alpha-\beta$, and \[ A_{m;\alpha,\beta} =\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal T_m^{+}(kN,kq). \] This is a normal Cohen--Macaulay graded domain of dimension $m^2-3$. Its graded canonical module satisfies \begin{equation} (\omega_{A_{m;\alpha,\beta}})_k \cong \mathcal T_m^{\eta_m}(kN-2r,kq-2). \end{equation} Its Hilbert function \[ F_{\alpha,\beta}(k) =\dim\left(S_{(k\alpha,k\beta)}\mathfrak{sl}_m\right) ^{\mathrm{PGL}_m\rtimes\langle\tau\rangle} \] is a quasipolynomial at every $k\ge0$, has degree $m^2-4$, and obeys \begin{equation} (-1)^{m^2-4}F_{\alpha,\beta}(-k) = \dim\mathcal T_m^{\eta_m}(kN-2r,kq-2) \qquad(k\ge1). \end{equation} Equivalently, the reciprocal space is the $\eta_m$ sector of \[ \left(S_{(k\alpha-r-1,\ k\beta-r+1)} \mathfrak{sl}_m\right)^{\mathrm{PGL}_m}, \] interpreted as zero unless the pair is an integral partition.

label: cor:all-stable-two-row-tail-reciprocity
statement: Suppose $m\ge3$ and $\alpha\ge\beta\ge0$. Every stable determinant ray \[ \lambda=(md-\alpha-\beta,\alpha,\beta),\qquad d\ge\alpha+\beta \] satisfies \begin{equation} 0\le(-1)^{\deg F}F(-k)\le F(k)\qquad(k\ge1). \end{equation}

label: prop:canonical-embedding-hstar
statement: Let $A$ be a finitely generated positively graded normal Cohen--Macaulay domain over $\mathbb C$, with $A_0=\mathbb C$ and dimension $n\ge2$. Suppose $a(A)<0$ and there is a degree-zero graded injection $\omega_A\hookrightarrow A$. Write $H=H_A$, $K=H_{\omega_A}$, and \[ \ell=\min\{j:(\omega_A)_j\ne0\}>0. \] For every sufficiently divisible positive integer $Q$, the three polynomials \[ h_Q(t)=(1-t^Q)^nH(t), \] \[ a_Q(t)=(1-t^Q)^{n-1}\bigl(H(t)-K(t)\bigr), \qquad b_Q(t)=(1-t^Q)^{n-1}\bigl(t^{-\ell}K(t)-H(t)\bigr) \] have nonnegative integer coefficients. They satisfy \begin{equation} \frac{1-t^\ell}{1-t^Q}h_Q(t) =a_Q(t)+t^\ell b_Q(t), \end{equation} and, with $E=Q(n-1)$, \begin{equation} t^Ea_Q(t^{-1})=a_Q(t),\qquad t^{E-\ell}b_Q(t^{-1})=b_Q(t). \end{equation} Moreover $a_Q(0)=h_Q(0)=1$ and $\deg h_Q=Qn-\ell$. The symmetry statements allow zero coefficients at the formal endpoints, and $b_Q$ may be identically zero.

label: lem:finite-equivariant-canonical-gate
statement: Let $R$ be a positively graded Cohen--Macaulay $\mathbb C$-domain and $\Gamma$ a finite group of graded automorphisms. Give $\omega_R$ its natural equivariant graded structure. Then \[ \omega_{R^\Gamma}\cong(\omega_R)^\Gamma. \] In particular, a degree-zero $\Gamma$-equivariant injection $\omega_R\hookrightarrow R$ induces a degree-zero canonical embedding for $R^\Gamma$.

label: prop:twisted-two-row-adjoint-gate
statement: Let $m\ge4$, $\alpha\ge\beta>0$, and $\gamma\in\{1,-1\}$. The function \[ f_\gamma(k)= \dim\left(S_{(k\alpha,k\beta)}V\right)^ {\mathrm{PGL}_m,\ \tau=\gamma^k} \qquad(k\ge0) \] is the Hilbert function of a normal Cohen--Macaulay graded domain with negative $a$-invariant and a degree-zero canonical embedding. Consequently it satisfies elementary Ehrhart reciprocity and the sufficiently divisible denominator conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-embedding-hstar}.

label: cor:stable-complement-two-row-tail-gate
statement: Let $m\ge4$ and $u\ge\alpha\ge\beta\ge0$ be integers. Omit zero parts from the partition \[ \rho=(u^{\,r-2},\,u-\beta,\,u-\alpha), \qquad |\rho|=ru-\alpha-\beta. \] In the stable chamber $d\ge\max(1,|\rho|)$, the determinant ray with \[ \lambda=(md-|\rho|,\rho) \] passes elementary Ehrhart reciprocity. If $\beta>0$, it also passes the sufficiently divisible denominator conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-embedding-hstar}. If $\beta=0$, its Hilbert function has an explicit rational polytope realization.

label: thm:adjoint-triple-rectangular-canonical
statement: The normal Cohen--Macaulay graded domain $A_m$ has dimension \[ n=2m^2-10=2r-8. \] Its canonical module satisfies \begin{equation} (\omega_{A_m})_a\cong B_{m,a-r}^{\,(-1)^r}. \end{equation} There is a degree-zero injection $\omega_{A_m}\hookrightarrow A_m$. For every integer $a\ge1$, the function \[ f_a(k)=\dim B_{m,ak}^{+} \] is a pure quasipolynomial of degree $2m^2-11$, and \begin{equation} (-1)^{2m^2-11}f_a(-k) =\dim B_{m,ak-r}^{\,(-1)^r} \le f_a(k)\qquad(k\ge1). \end{equation} Every such ray also satisfies the sufficiently divisible denominator conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-embedding-hstar}.

label: thm:growing-rectangular-canonical
statement: Let $h\ge24$ and $m\ge h+5$. Put \[ r=m^2-1,\qquad V=\mathfrak{sl}_m,\qquad B_{m,h}=\mathbb C[V\otimes\mathbb C^h] ^{\mathrm{PGL}_m\times\mathrm{SL}_h},\qquad A_{m,h}=B_{m,h}^{\langle\tau\rangle}, \] where $\tau$ simultaneously transposes the matrices. Grade these rings by ordinary polynomial degree divided by $h$, and write $B_{m,h,j}^{\epsilon}$ for the degree-$j$ transpose eigenspace of sign $\epsilon$. Negative-degree pieces are understood to be zero. Set \[ \delta=(-1)^{m(m-1)/2},\qquad \eta=(-1)^r\delta^{h-1},\qquad D=(h-1)r-h^2+1. \] Then $A_{m,h}$ and $B_{m,h}$ are normal Cohen--Macaulay domains of dimension $D$, and \begin{equation} (\omega_{A_{m,h}})_j\cong B_{m,h,j-r}^{\eta}. \end{equation} Both $B_{m,h,1}^{+}$ and $B_{m,h,1}^{-}$ are nonzero, and there is a degree-zero graded injection \[ \omega_{A_{m,h}}\hookrightarrow A_{m,h}. \] Moreover, \[ a(A_{m,h})= \begin{cases} -r,&\eta=1,\\ -(r+1),&\eta=-1. \end{cases} \] Its Hilbert function $f$ is a pure quasipolynomial for all nonnegative integers, and $f(k)>0$ for every $k\ge0$. For every integer $a\ge1$, the Veronese $C_a=A_{m,h}^{(a)}$ has a degree-zero canonical embedding and first nonzero canonical degree \begin{equation} \ell_a=-a(C_a) =\left\lceil\frac{r+(1-\eta)/2}{a}\right\rceil>0. \end{equation} Writing $F_a(k)=f(ak)$, its quasipolynomial extension satisfies \begin{equation} 0\le(-1)^{D-1}F_a(-k) =\dim B_{m,h,ak-r}^{\eta}\le F_a(k) \qquad(k\ge1). \end{equation} Each Veronese satisfies the sufficiently divisi

label: cor:growing-veronese-numerators
statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:growing-rectangular-canonical}, fix $a\ge1$. Write $C=C_a$, $H=H_C$, $K=H_{\omega_C}$, and $\ell=\ell_a$ as in \eqref{eq:growing-veronese-canonical-degree}. There is a positive integer $Q_0$ such that, for every positive multiple $Q$ of $Q_0$, the three polynomials \begin{align} h_Q(t)&=(1-t^Q)^D H(t),\notag\\ a_Q(t)&=(1-t^Q)^{D-1}\bigl(H(t)-K(t)\bigr),\\ b_Q(t)&=(1-t^Q)^{D-1}\bigl(t^{-\ell}K(t)-H(t)\bigr)\notag \end{align} have nonnegative integer coefficients. With $E=Q(D-1)$, \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \frac{1-t^\ell}{1-t^Q}h_Q(t)=a_Q(t)+t^\ell b_Q(t), \\ t^E a_Q(t^{-1})=a_Q(t),\qquad t^{E-\ell}b_Q(t^{-1})=b_Q(t). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Also $a_Q(0)=h_Q(0)=1$ and $\deg h_Q=QD-\ell$. Zero coefficients at the formal symmetry endpoints are allowed, and $b_Q$ may be zero. In particular, putting $S_Q(t)=1+t+\cdots+t^{Q-1}$ gives \[ (1+t+\cdots+t^{\ell-1})h_Q =(S_Qa_Q)+t^\ell(S_Qb_Q), \] whose two nonnegative symmetric polynomials have formal symmetry degrees $QD-1$ and $QD-1-\ell$. These are the sufficiently divisible numerator conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-embedding-hstar}.

label: cor:growing-rectangular-determinant-gate
statement: Let $h\ge24$, $m\ge h+5$, $a\ge1$, and $d\ge ah$. For the full determinant-stabilizer ray with \[ \lambda=(md-ah,a^h), \] elementary Ehrhart reciprocity and the sufficiently divisible denominator conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-embedding-hstar} hold. More precisely, its stretched multiplicity is the positive pure quasipolynomial $F_a$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:growing-rectangular-canonical}, and its sufficiently divisible numerators have all the properties in Corollary~\ref{cor:growing-veronese-numerators}. In particular this applies to $h=n^2$, $n\ge5$, $m\ge n^{25}$, and to the trace-cubic specialization $a=3/\gcd(n^2,3)$.

label: lem:negative-canonical-character-poles
statement: Let $S$ be a positively graded complex Cohen--Macaulay Gorenstein domain of dimension $D$, with $S_0=\mathbb C$, and let $\tau$ be a degree-preserving involution. Suppose that, equivariantly, \[ \omega_S\simeq S(-R)\otimes\operatorname{sgn}, \] where $\tau$ acts as $-1$ on $\operatorname{sgn}$. Write $H_\pm(t)=\sum_{k\geq0}\dim S_k^\pm t^k$. Then \[ H_+(t^{-1})=(-1)^D t^R H_-(t),\qquad H_-(t^{-1})=(-1)^D t^R H_+(t). \] The two series have the same pole order at every root of unity. Consequently every ordinary Hilbert pole of $S$ is an ordinary Hilbert pole of $S^\tau$, with at least the same order.

label: cor:trace-cubic-connected-pole-reduction
statement: Let $h\geq24$, $m\geq h+5$, and $m\equiv4\pmod {12}$. Set $r=m^2-1$, $a=3/\gcd(h,3)$, and \[ B=\mathbb C[\mathfrak{sl}_m\otimes\mathbb C^h] ^{PGL_m\times SL_h},\qquad S=B^{(a)},\qquad \mathcal T_{m,h}=(B^\tau)^{(a)}, \] where $B$ is graded by ordinary degree divided by $h$. Every ordinary Hilbert pole of $S$ survives in $\mathcal T_{m,h}$, with at least the same order. In particular this applies to the determinant ray of Corollary~\ref{cor:growing-rectangular-determinant-gate} with $\lambda=(md-ah,a^h)$ and $d\geq ah$, and to its subfamily $h=n^2$, $n\geq5$, $m\geq n^{25}$, $m\equiv4\pmod {12}$.

label: prop:negative-character-index-barrier
statement: For every integer $L\geq2$, there is a positively graded normal Gorenstein domain $S_L$ with rational singularities and a degree-preserving involution $\tau$ such that \[ \omega_{S_L}\simeq S_L(-1)\otimes\operatorname{sgn}, \] but the strict indices of its Hilbert function $f_L$ and that of its invariant ring $f_L^+$ satisfy \[ p(f_L)=\left\lfloor\frac{L-1}{2}\right\rfloor, \qquad s(f_L)=\left\lfloor\frac{L-2}{2}\right\rfloor, \qquad p(f_L^+)=s(f_L^+)=0. \] Thus the ordinary-pole transfer in Lemma~\ref{lem:negative-canonical-character-poles} does not by itself transfer a strict-index lower bound.

label: thm:central-matrix-net-canonical
statement: For $m\ge4$, $A_m$ is a normal Cohen--Macaulay graded domain of dimension $m^2-6$, with \begin{equation} (\omega_{A_m})_k\cong C_{m,k-m}^{\eta_m}. \end{equation} Before the finite transpose quotient, the connected invariant ring has the equivariant canonical description \begin{equation} (\omega_{R_m})_N \cong R_{m,N-3m^2}\otimes\mathbb C_{\eta_m}, \end{equation} where the second factor records the natural transpose action. Consequently every $F_{m,a}$ is a pure quasipolynomial of degree $m^2-7$, and \begin{equation} (-1)^{m^2-7}F_{m,a}(-k) =\dim C_{m,ak-m}^{\eta_m} \qquad(k\ge1). \end{equation}

label: lem:matrix-net-koszul-invariant
statement: For every $m\ge2$, the polynomial \begin{equation} K_m(X_1,X_2,X_3)= \det\begin{pmatrix} 0&X_3&-X_2\\ -X_3&0&X_1\\ X_2&-X_1&0 \end{pmatrix} \end{equation} is a nonzero element of $C_{m,1}^{\,(-1)^m}$.

label: lem:double-rectangle-transpose-sector
statement: Let $p,q$ be positive integers with $N=pq$ divisible by three. For both signs $\epsilon$, \begin{equation} \dim R_{p,N}^{\epsilon}=\dim R_{q,N}^{\epsilon}. \end{equation} Here both rings have third tensor factor $\mathbb C^3$ and the same ordinary degree $N$.

label: lem:matrix-net-odd-character-seeds
statement: For the connected matrix-net invariant ring at size six, \[ \dim R_{6,36}^-=7,\qquad \dim R_{6,42}^-=41. \] More precisely, the total dimension, transpose trace, and the two eigenspace dimensions are \[ \begin{array}{c|r|r|r|r|r} N&\text{cycle types}&\dim R_{6,N}&\operatorname{tr}\tau &\dim R_{6,N}^+&\dim R_{6,N}^-\\\hline 36&17977&58&44&51&7\\ 42&53174&189&107&148&41 \end{array}. \]

label: cor:matrix-net-small-odd-multiplier
statement: For every $m\ge6$ there is a nonzero transpose-odd invariant \[ v_m\in R_{m,6m}^-=C_{m,2}^-. \]

label: thm:eventual-central-matrix-net-gate
statement: For every $m\ge6$ and every $a\ge1$, the central determinant ray $F_{m,a}$ satisfies elementary Ehrhart reciprocity: \begin{equation} 0\le(-1)^{m^2-7}F_{m,a}(-k)\le F_{m,a}(k) \qquad(k\ge1). \end{equation} In fact $A_m$ has a degree-zero canonical embedding, as does every Veronese, and it satisfies the sufficiently divisible denominator conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-embedding-hstar}.

label: prop:noncentral-two-equal-canonical
statement: The ray algebra \[ A_{m;\alpha,\beta} =\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal U_m^+(kN,kq) \] is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain of dimension $m^2-4$. Its canonical module is \begin{equation} (\omega_A)_k \cong\mathcal U_m^{\eta_m}(kN-3m^2,kq-3). \end{equation} Thus its Hilbert function $F$ is a pure quasipolynomial of degree $m^2-5$, with \begin{equation} (-1)^{m^2-5}F(-k) =\dim\left( S_{(k\alpha-m^2-2,\, k\beta-m^2+1,\, k\beta-m^2+1)} (\mathbb C^m\otimes\mathbb C^m) \right)^{\mathrm{SL}_m\times\mathrm{SL}_m,\, \tau=\eta_m}. \end{equation}

label: prop:kappa-even-nonvanishing
statement: For every even $m\ge6$, \begin{equation} F_{\kappa_m}(1)>0, \qquad \kappa_m=(m^2+2,m^2-1,m^2-1),\quad d=3m. \end{equation} In particular, the proposed hole at $k=1$ does not occur for $m\equiv2\pmod4$ in the range $m\ge4$.

label: cor:kappa-positive-canonical-embedding
statement: Let $m\ge4$ with $m\equiv1,2\pmod4$, and let \[ A=A_{m;m^2+2,m^2-1} =\bigoplus_{k\ge0}\mathcal U_m^+(3m^2k,3k). \] Then $\omega_A\cong A(-1)$ and there is a degree-zero injection $\omega_A\hookrightarrow A$. Every stretch and every Veronese of this ray therefore satisfies elementary Ehrhart reciprocity.

label: thm:strict-three-row-canonical
statement: Let $m\ge4$, $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\lambda_3>0$, and $|\lambda|=md$. Let $A_\lambda$ be the full determinant-stabilizer ray algebra, so that $\dim(A_\lambda)_k=F_\lambda(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$. Then $A_\lambda$ is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain of dimension $m^2-3$, and its graded canonical module has components \begin{equation} (\omega_{A_\lambda})_k \cong\mathcal M_m^{\eta_m}(k\lambda-\kappa_m). \end{equation} The identification respects the highest-weight multiplication defining the ray and its canonical module. Its Hilbert function is a pure quasipolynomial on all nonnegative integers, and \begin{equation} (-1)^{m^2-4}F_\lambda(-k) =\dim\mathcal M_m^{\eta_m}(k\lambda-\kappa_m) \qquad(k\ge1). \end{equation}

label: lem:full-flag-explicit-covariants
statement: For every even $m\ge4$, the matrix invariant ring has a nonzero transpose-even label component of shape $(m+2,m,m-2)$ in ordinary degree $3m$. For every odd $m\ge3$, it has a nonzero transpose-even label component of shape $(2m+2,2m,2m-2)$ in ordinary degree $6m$.

label: thm:strict-three-row-canonical-embedding
statement: Let $\lambda_1>\lambda_2>\lambda_3>0$ and $|\lambda|=md$. For every $m\ge6$, the full determinant ray algebra $A_\lambda$ has a degree-zero canonical embedding. Every such ray, and every Veronese, satisfies \[ 0\le(-1)^{m^2-4}F_\lambda(-k)\le F_\lambda(k)\qquad(k\ge1) \] and the sufficiently divisible numerator conditions of Proposition~\ref{prop:canonical-embedding-hstar}.

label: prop:trace-cubic-retraction
statement: There are $GL(W)$-equivariant algebra homomorphisms \[ \mathbb C[\operatorname{Sym}^3W^*] \xrightarrow{\ \iota\ }\mathcal A_{m,h}^{\tau} \xrightarrow{\ \rho\ } \mathbb C[\operatorname{Sym}^3W^*] \] with $\rho\iota=1$. A cubic-coefficient polynomial of degree $d$ is sent by $\iota$ to a matrix-entry polynomial of degree $3d$. Conversely $\rho$ sends a matrix-entry homogeneous polynomial of degree $e$ to a cubic-coefficient polynomial of degree $e/3$, and sends it to zero if $3\nmid e$.

label: cor:trace-retraction-parameters
statement: Every homogeneous system of parameters of $\mathcal T_{m,h}$ contains an element of degree at least $2^{h-1}$. The same lower bound holds for the largest degree in every homogeneous algebra generating set.

label: prop:retract-pole-counterexample
statement: For every integer $M\ge2$, there is a three-dimensional positively graded normal toric domain $R_M$ with rational singularities and an exposed-face algebra retract $S_M=\mathbb C[u]$, $\deg u=M$, such that \[ H_{R_M}(t)=\frac{1+(M-2)t}{(1-t)^3},\qquad H_{S_M}(t)=\frac1{1-t^M}. \] Every homogeneous generating set and every homogeneous system of parameters of $R_M$ contains an element of degree at least $M$. Nevertheless its Hilbert function is the polynomial \[ h_M(k)=\frac{M-1}{2}k^2+\frac{M+1}{2}k+1, \] so both strict indices are zero and a numerical positive rational form has all denominator weights equal to one.

Let $A=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}A_k$ be a finitely generated positively graded complex algebra with $A_0=\mathbb C$. Its universal module denominator $U_A(t)$ is the least common multiple of the reduced Hilbert-series denominators of all homogeneous ideals $I\subseteq A$, including $I=A$, normalized to have constant coefficient one. Equivalently it clears the Hilbert series of every finitely generated graded $A$-module.

label: cor:determinant-universal-module-denominator
statement: Let $h\ge4$, $g=\gcd(h,3)$, $a=3/g$, and $m\ge2h+1$. Choose any $d\ge ah$ and set \[ \lambda=(md-ah,a^h),\qquad M=2^{h-1}. \] Let $\mathcal R_{m,d,\lambda}$ be the determinant-stabilizer stretching algebra, with its degree-$k$ piece of dimension $m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$ and with its highest-weight Cartan multiplication. Then \[ \Phi_M(t)\mid U_{\mathcal R_{m,d,\lambda}}(t), \qquad \deg U_{\mathcal R_{m,d,\lambda}}\ge\varphi(M)=2^{h-2}. \] This does not assert that $\Phi_M$ divides the reduced denominator of $H_{\mathcal R_{m,d,\lambda}}$ itself.

label: cor:module-denominator-gct-range
statement: For every integer $n\ge2$ and every $m\ge2n^2+1$, set \[ h=n^2,\quad g=\gcd(n^2,3),\quad d=\frac{3n^2}{g},\quad \lambda=\left(d(m-1),\left(\frac3g\right)^{n^2}\right). \] Then $\lambda$ has height $n^2+1$, and the determinant-stabilizer stretching algebra has a universal module denominator of degree at least $2^{n^2-2}$. In particular this degree is not bounded by any fixed polynomial in $m$ on the family $m=n^{25}$.

label: lem:trace-cubic-irreducible
statement: Let $\dim W=h\geq2$, and let $F\in\operatorname{Sym}^3W^*$ be concise: the condition $F(v,-,-)=0$ implies $v=0$. On $E=\mathbb C\oplus W\oplus W^*$ define \[ A_F(x)(a,v,\ell)=\bigl(\ell(x),ax,F(x,v,-)\bigr). \] The tuple $A_F$ is irreducible. In particular its simultaneous conjugation orbit is closed and its stabilizer in $PGL(E)$ is trivial.

label: lem:dyadic-chain-quadratic-bound
statement: Let $q=2^\ell$ with $\ell\geq2$, and let $(\mu_a)_{a\in\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z}$ be nonnegative real numbers of total mass $m$. Then \[ Q_\ell(\mu):= \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\sum_{a\in\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z} \mu_a\mu_{a+2^i}\leq\frac{m^2}{2}. \] Equality holds exactly when the support lies in a coset of the subgroup of order four and, in cyclic order on that coset, the masses are $(x,y,x,y)$ for some $x,y\geq0$. Replacing any shift $2^i$ by $-2^i$ leaves $Q_\ell$ unchanged.

label: cor:dyadic-chain-fixed-tangent-bound
statement: Let $h\geq4$, $q=2^{h-1}$, and $b_i=(-2)^i\pmod q$ for $0\leq i\leq h-2$, with $b_{h-1}=0$. Suppose a tuple in $\mathfrak{sl}_m^h$ has a closed orbit and trivial stabilizer for $PGL_m\times SL_h$. Suppose moreover that it is fixed by a grading lift whose label transformation has the distinct eigenweights $b_i$, and whose matrix conjugation transformation has $q$th-root eigenweights of multiplicities $\mu_a$. The corresponding smooth joint quotient has fixed tangent dimension \[ Q_{h-1}(\mu)-h+1 <\frac{m^2}{2}-h+1. \] For even $m$ this is at most $m^2/2-h$.

label: lem:leading-residue-prime-poles
statement: Let $H(t)\in\mathbb Z[[t]]\cap\mathbb Q(t)$ have only roots of unity as poles, and let its pole at $1$ have order $n$. Write its reduced denominator as \[ (1-t)^n\prod_{d>1}\Phi_d(t)^{h_d} \] and put \[ e=\lim_{t\to1}(1-t)^nH(t)\ne0. \] If $b$ is the positive denominator of $e$ in lowest terms, then for every prime $p$, \begin{equation} v_p(b)\le\sum_{a\ge1}h_{p^a}. \end{equation} In particular, every prime dividing $b$ forces a genuine prime-power pole of the reduced numerical series. If all roots of unity that are poles have multiplicative order at most $L$ and $p^2>L$, it forces a primitive $p$th-root pole, of pole multiplicity at least $v_p(b)$.

label: lem:actual-wave-positivity-gate
statement: Suppose $H$ has a unique pole of maximal order $n$, located at $1$, and has $J$ distinct poles. Write its proper partial-fraction expansion as \[ H(t)=\sum_{\zeta}\sum_{s=1}^{n_\zeta} A_{\zeta,s}(1-t/\zeta)^{-s}. \] Let $e=A_{1,n}>0$. Suppose $C\ge1$ satisfies \begin{equation} |A_{\zeta,s}|/e\le C^{\,n-s} \quad\text{for every }(\zeta,s). \end{equation} Then every constituent of the coefficient quasipolynomial becomes coefficientwise positive after any integer shift \begin{equation} c\ge 6Jn\max(C,n). \end{equation}

label: thm:nullcone-strict-index-bound
statement: Let \[ R=\bigoplus_{k\geq 0}R_k \] be a finitely generated positively graded Cohen--Macaulay domain over \(\mathbb C\), with \(R_0=\mathbb C\), Krull dimension \(n\geq 1\), and \(a(R)<0\). Suppose homogeneous elements of positive degrees at most an integer \(S\geq 1\) have common zero set equal to the vertex of \(\operatorname{Spec}R\). Then \[ f(k)=\dim_{\mathbb C}R_k \] is a pure quasipolynomial and \[ s(f)\leq p(f)\leq 202\,n^4S^6. \] Moreover, for every integer \(a\geq 1\), the sampled function \(f_a(k)=f(ak)\) is a pure quasipolynomial and satisfies \[ s(f_a)\leq p(f_a)\leq 202\,n^4S^6. \] No primitivity assumption on the grading is required.

label: prop:identity-pole-control
statement: Let $R$ be a positively graded Cohen--Macaulay domain over $\mathbb C$, with $R_0=\mathbb C$, dimension $n\ge1$, and $a(R)<0$. Suppose homogeneous elements of degrees at most the positive integer $S$ have common zero set equal to the vertex of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Write the principal part of its Hilbert series at $1$ as \[ H_R(t)=\sum_{s=1}^n A_{1,s}(1-t)^{-s} +\text{a function regular at }1, \qquad e=A_{1,n}>0. \] Then, for $0\le j<n$, \begin{equation} \frac{|A_{1,n-j}|}{e}\le(5nS^2)^j. \end{equation} The corresponding polynomial contribution \[ P(x)=\sum_{s=1}^n A_{1,s}\binom{x+s-1}{s-1} \] has strictly positive coefficients after every integer shift \begin{equation} c\ge30n^2S^2. \end{equation} All actual poles have multiplicative order at most $S$; in particular, their number $J$ satisfies \begin{equation} J\le\sum_{q=1}^S\varphi(q)\le S(S+1)/2. \end{equation}

label: cor:stable-rectangular-tail-strict-indices
statement: For $m\ge3$, $a\ge1$ and $d\ge2a$, the full determinant ray $\lambda=(md-2a,a,a)$ satisfies \[ s(F)\le p(F)<2^{20}m^{56}. \]

label: thm:two-row-transpose-sector-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $\alpha\ge\beta\ge0$, and $\gamma\in\{1,-1\}$. Put $V=\mathfrak{sl}_m$ and \begin{equation} F(k)=\dim\bigl(S_{(k\alpha,k\beta)}V\bigr) ^{\mathrm{PGL}_m,\,\tau=\gamma^k}. \end{equation} Then \[ s(F)\le p(F)<2^{44}m^{224}. \] The bound is uniform in $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ and applies to every Veronese. If $\alpha=\beta=0$, both indices are zero.

label: cor:stable-two-row-tail-strict-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $\alpha\ge\beta\ge0$, and $d\ge\max(1,\alpha+\beta)$. For the full determinant-stabilizer ray associated with $\lambda=(md-\alpha-\beta,\alpha,\beta)$, one has \[ s(F)\le p(F)<2^{44}m^{224}. \] The bound is uniform in $\alpha,\beta,d$ and applies to every Veronese.

label: thm:complementary-two-row-strict-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, put $r=m^2-1$, and let $u\ge\alpha\ge\beta\ge0$ be integers. Delete zero parts from \[ \rho=(u^{r-2},u-\beta,u-\alpha). \] For $d\ge\max(1,|\rho|)$ and $\lambda=(md-|\rho|,\rho)$, the full determinant-stabilizer ray $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$ satisfies \[ s(F)\le p(F)<2^{44}m^{224}. \] The bound is uniform in $u,\alpha,\beta,d$ and applies to every Veronese of the ray.

label: cor:nearly-full-rectangular-strict-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $r=m^2-1$, $a\ge1$, $h\in\{r-2,r-1,r\}$, and $d\ge ah$. For $\lambda=(md-ah,a^h)$ and $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$, one has \[ \begin{array}{c|c} h&\text{strict-index bound}\\\hline r-2&s(F)\le p(F)<2^{20}m^{56},\\ r-1&s(F)\le p(F)<2^{14}m^{10},\\ r&s(F)=p(F)=0. \end{array} \]

label: prop:trace-cubic-vertex-cutoff
statement: Let $h\ge4$, $g=\gcd(h,3)$, $a=3/g$, $m\ge2h+1$, and $d\ge ah$. Let $R_{m,h}$ be the full determinant-stabilizer ray algebra for $\lambda=(md-ah,a^h)$, graded by the stretch. If homogeneous elements of degrees at most $S$ have common zero set equal to its vertex, then \[ S\ge2^{h-1}. \]

label: lem:multigraded-ray-generator-bound
statement: Let $A$ be an $\mathbb N^h$-graded algebra with $A_0=\mathbb C$. Suppose it is generated by homogeneous elements whose nonzero degree vectors have sum of coordinates at most an integer $B\ge1$. For any nonzero $v\in\mathbb N^h$, the algebra \[ A(v)=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}A_{kv}, \] graded by $k$, is generated in degrees at most \[ (B+1)^h B^h\le 2^hB^{2h}. \] The vector $v$ need not be primitive. Moreover, homogeneous elements of ray degrees at most $B^h$ have common zero set equal to the vertex of $\operatorname{Spec}A(v)$.

label: thm:all-three-row-strict-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $d\ge1$, and $\lambda\vdash md$ with at most three rows. For the full determinant-stabilizer ray $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$, one has \[ s(F)\le p(F) \le202(3m^2+8)^4(B_m^3)^6 \le101\cdot2^{27}3^{54}m^{692}\le m^{769}. \] The bound is uniform in $d$ and $\lambda$ and also holds for every Veronese of the ray. No stability condition on the first row is imposed.

label: thm:fixed-height-all-rays-strict-indices
statement: Let \(m\geq3\), \(2\leq h\leq m^2\), \(d\geq1\), and let \(\lambda\vdash md\) have at most \(h\) parts. For the full determinant-stabilizer stretching function \(F(k)=m_{k\lambda}^{kd}\), \begin{equation} s(F)\leq p(F) <(2mh)^{72h^3-9h+17} <m^{288h^3}. \end{equation} The bounds are uniform in \(\lambda,d\), and hold for every Veronese. One-row rays have \(s(F)=p(F)=0\).

label: cor:determinant-complement-height
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $N=m^2$, and let $\lambda\vdash md$ be padded with zeros to $N$ parts. Let $u$ be the multiplicity of its smallest part and $r$ that of its largest part, and put \[ h_* =\min(N-u,N-r). \] For the full determinant-stabilizer ray $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$, if $h_*\ge2$, then \[ s(F)\le p(F)<(2mh_*)^{72h_*^3-9h_*+17}. \] If $h_*=0$ or $1$, both strict indices are zero. All these conclusions hold uniformly for every Veronese.

label: cor:rectangular-determinant-strict-indices
statement: Let $m\ge3$, $2\le h\le m^2$, and $u\ge1$, with $m$ dividing $hu$. For $\lambda=(u^h)$, $d=hu/m$, and $F(k)=m^{kd}_{k\lambda}$, put $L=m(m-1)$. Then \[ s(F)\le p(F) \le12928\,m^8h^4L^{6h^2} <m^{12h^2+25}. \] The bound is uniform in $u$ and holds for every Veronese.

label: prop:varying-rank-ray-obstruction
statement: For every integer $r\ge1$, put $\ell=2r+1$. There is a polynomial ring $R_r$ in $\ell+2$ variables with a nonnegative $\mathbb Z^{\ell+1}$ grading such that every variable has first coordinate one, every generator multidegree has sum at most $\ell+3$, and the ray algebra \[ A_r=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}(R_r)_{k(1,1,\ldots,1)} \] is a weighted polynomial ring in two variables of degrees \[ a=2^{r+1}-1,\qquad b=2^{r+1}. \] In particular it is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain with faithful grading and negative $a$-invariant, but its Hilbert function satisfies \begin{equation} s(F_r)=p(F_r)=ab-a-b =2^{2r+2}-3\cdot2^{r+1}+1. \end{equation} Thus no bound polynomial jointly in the number of grading coordinates, ambient dimension, and generator multidegree sum holds for the strict indices of arbitrary rays, even under all the displayed hypotheses and even when every ray-coordinate ratio is one.

label: thm:broad-density-failure
statement: Let $A(N)$ count positive-initial inputs in this product-closed subgroup-restriction population, and let $E(N)$ count the inputs among them with nonzero strict saturation index. There is a constant $C$ such that \[ E(N+C)\ge A(N). \] Consequently $E(N)/A(N)$ cannot be eventually at most $N^{-c}$ for every fixed $c>0$. This disproves the broad density assertion under the stated finite, additive specification convention.

label: thm:fixed-embedding-density
statement: Fix $n\ge2$ and a polynomial highest weight $\mu$ of $GL_n$, and put $d=|\mu|$ and $m=\dim S_\mu\mathbb C^n$. Assume $m>n$. Among the ordinary plethysm inputs $(\lambda,\mu,\pi)$ satisfying \[ \operatorname{ht}(\lambda)\le m,\quad \operatorname{ht}(\pi)\le n,\quad a_{\lambda,\mu}^{\pi}>0,\quad \ell(\lambda)+\ell(\mu)+\ell(\pi)=N, \] the proportion with $s(a_{s\lambda,\mu}^{s\pi})>0$ is \[ O_{n,\mu}(N^{m+n-1}2^{-\eta_{n,\mu}N}) \] for some $\eta_{n,\mu}>0$. The denominator of this proportion is nonzero for every sufficiently large $N$.

label: lem:polynomial-sublevel
statement: Let $P$ be a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree $e\ge1$ on $\mathbb R^r$ and let $\Lambda$ be a full lattice. For fixed $A,C>0$, \[ \#\{u\in\Lambda:\|u\|\le CR,\ |P(u)|\le AR^{e-1}\} =O(R^{r-1/e}). \]

label: lem:chamber-density
statement: Suppose a nonnegative lattice function on a full-dimensional cone in $\mathbb R^r$ has a finite conic piecewise quasipolynomial formula that gives the global constituents on each ray. Let $e_*$ be the maximum of one and the degrees of its nonzero full-dimensional constituent polynomials. Its inputs of norm at most $R$ with a nonzero strict saturation index number $O(R^{r-1/e_*})$.

A partition $\lambda$ is an occurrence obstruction if $K_n(\lambda)=0<q_\lambda$, and a multiplicity obstruction if $K_n(\lambda)<q_\lambda$. The latter definition allows both multiplicities to be positive.

label: thm:full-family
statement: Let $n\geq3$, $N=n^2$, $Q=N(n-2)$, and let $u,a,k$ be integers with $u\geq0$ and $a\geq k\geq0$. Put \begin{equation} \begin{split} d&=a+uN,\\ \Lambda&=(na+u(Q+2)-k,\;2u+k,\;(2u)^{N-2}). \end{split} \end{equation} Zero terminal parts are omitted. Then $\Lambda\vdash nd$ and \begin{align} K_n(\Lambda) &=\sk(\Lambda,(d^n)) =g(\Lambda,(d^n),(d^n))=h_n(k),\\ q_\Lambda&\geq\sum_{j=0}^{\min(u,k)}h_n(k-j). \end{align} The lower bound is realized by the explicit highest-weight polynomials in \eqref{eq:explicit-family}. If $u=0$, the permanent multiplicity also equals $h_n(k)$. When $d=0$, the ambient, determinant, and permanent coordinate rings each have a one-dimensional space of constants.

label: cor:ray
statement: Fix $u,a\geq1$ and put $\mu=\Lambda(u,a,1)$. For every integer $s\geq1$, at coefficient degree $s(a+uN)$ one has \[ q_{s\mu}\geq p_n(s)>h_n(s)=K_n(s\mu). \] The determinant multiplicity vanishes only at $s=1$ among positive integer stretches. In particular, $\mu$ is a hole in the support semigroup relative to its generated group: $2\mu$ and $3\mu$ occur, $\mu=3\mu-2\mu$, and $\mu$ does not occur.

label: thm:large-padding
statement: Let $m\geq2$, $n\geq m^{25}$ and $\lambda\vdash nd$. For the independently padded permanent $z^{n-m}\per_m$, the inequality $q_\lambda>K_n(\lambda)$ implies \[ m\geq190,\qquad \ell(\lambda)\geq52,\qquad \lambda_{2j}\geq28-j\quad(1\leq j\leq26). \] In addition, $d\geq m^{12}+1$ and $\lambda_2>m^{23/2}$. More precisely, writing $t=\lambda_2$ and $T=|\lambda|-\lambda_1$, every gap requires $n<1+\min\{d,T\}(t-1)$. The same conclusions hold when a matrix entry supplies the padding. In particular $\lambda_2\geq27$, $\lambda_{27}\geq14$ and $\lambda_{52}\geq2$.

label: lem:binary-basis
statement: The functions $F_0,I_2,\ldots,I_n$ are highest-weight functions. The coefficient degree and highest weight of $I_i$ are $i$ and $(i(n-1),i)$, respectively. If $a\geq k$, the polynomials \begin{equation} F_0^{a-k}\prod_{i=2}^n I_i^{\alpha_i}, \qquad \alpha_i\geq0,\quad \sum_{i=2}^n i\alpha_i=k, \end{equation} form a basis of the highest-weight space of type $(na-k,k)$ in the binary coefficient ring. Their restrictions are independent on both $\Det_n$ and $\Perm_n$.

label: lem:det-hessian
statement: With ordinary second derivatives in the matrix-entry basis, one has \begin{equation} H(\det_n)=c_n\det_n^{t},\qquad t=n(n-2),\quad c_n=(-1)^{(n-1)(n+2)/2}(n-1). \end{equation} In particular $H_0$ is nonzero on $\Det_n$.

label: lem:block-hessian
statement: Let $s=n-2$, $t=n(n-2)$ and \[ X=\diag(B,z_1,\ldots,z_s),\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}. \] Put $p=ad+bc$, $\Delta=ad-bc$ and $E=\prod_i z_i$. Then \begin{equation} H(\per_n)(X)=c_n E^t p^{s^2}\Delta^{2s}. \end{equation} In particular, wherever $Ep\ne0$, \begin{equation} \frac{H(\per_n)(X)}{\per_n(X)^t} =c_n\left(\frac{\Delta}{p}\right)^{2s}. \end{equation}

label: lem:transcendence
statement: On the permanent orbit, the rational function $Z/H_0$ is transcendental over $\C(F_0,\ldots,F_n)$.

label: thm:cubic-complete
statement: In coordinate degree twelve, for the partition $\lambda=(19,7,2,2,2,2,2)$, the multiplicities in the ambient polynomial ring, the determinant orbit closure, and the permanent orbit closure are, respectively, \[ a_\lambda=6,\qquad K_3(\lambda)=5, \qquad q_\lambda=6. \] The six highest-weight functions defined below form a basis of the ambient multiplicity space. Its restriction kernel on the determinant closure is spanned by \[ \Psi=2P_0+21P_1+7P_2+35P_3+7P_4, \] and its restriction kernel on the permanent closure is zero.

label: thm:partial-basic
statement: For $2\le r<n^2$ the ambient and determinant multiplicities satisfy \[ a_{\lambda_{n,r}}(d_r[n])=K_n(\lambda_{n,r})=1. \] At $r=n^2$ the ambient multiplicity is one, the determinant multiplicity is zero, and the unpadded permanent multiplicity is one.

label: thm:partial-ray
statement: For $3\le r<n^2$, the functions $Z_r,U_2,\ldots,U_n$ are algebraically independent on $\Det_n$. Consequently \[ K_n(s\lambda_{n,r})\ge p_n(s) \qquad(s\ge0). \]

label: thm:jet-dominance
statement: Let $n\geq2$ and $2\leq r\leq2n$. The projection of determinantal forms in $r$ variables to $\mathcal J_{n,r}$ is dominant. The same is true for permanental forms of size $n$. Consequently restriction to $\Det_n$ is injective on the algebra generated by all coefficients of \[ F(x,y,0),\qquad H_r(F)(x,y,0), \] and by the coefficients of all Hessian minors in the first $r$ directions along this binary plane.

label: cor:algebra-limitation
statement: Let $2\leq r\leq2n$, and let $L$ be any finite-dimensional space of highest-weight functions of one degree and one weight contained in the coefficient algebra of Theorem~\ref{thm:jet-dominance}. For every form orbit closure $Y$, \[ \dim\operatorname{res}_Y L\leq\dim L =\dim\operatorname{res}_{\Det_n}L \leq K_n(\wt L). \] Thus the copies furnished by this whole coefficient algebra cannot establish a strict multiplicity advantage over the determinant.

label: prop:padding
statement: Let $1\leq m<n$, and let $q^{\mathrm{pad}}_\lambda$ denote the multiplicity for the orbit closure of $z^{n-m}\per_m$, where $z$ is independent of the permanent entries. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item $q^{\mathrm{pad}}_\lambda=0$ if $\ell(\lambda)>m^2+1$. In particular every type in Theorem~\ref{thm:full-family} with $u>0$ has padded permanent multiplicity zero. \item Every basic partial-Hessian bracket type $\lambda_{n,r}$, $2\leq r\leq n^2$, satisfies $q^{\mathrm{pad}}_{\lambda_{n,r}}\leq K_n(\lambda_{n,r})$. \item If $m^2+1\leq2n$, the whole binary coefficient algebra of every potentially useful partial Hessian is covered by Corollary~\ref{cor:algebra-limitation}. \end{enumerate} If the padding variable is a permanent entry, replace $m^2+1$ by $m^2$ in these assertions.

label: lem:nested-support
statement: If $P\in\Sym^d\Sym^n\C^r$ is a highest-weight polynomial of weight $\lambda$, every coefficient generator $f_\eta$ occurring in $P$ satisfies \[ |\eta|=n,\qquad \eta_j+\cdots+\eta_r\leq\lambda_j \quad(2\leq j\leq r). \] The assertion concerns each generator in each monomial of $P$.

label: lem:two-trees
statement: Let $f$ be any degree-$m$ form in $r$ variables, one of which is $L$. Split the other variables into sets of sizes $p$ and $q$, where $p+q=r-1$. Put \[ S=\binom{m+p}{p}+\binom{m+q}{q}-1. \] If $n\geq\max\{m,S\}$, then $L^{n-m}f$ is the determinant of an $n$ by $n$ homogeneous linear matrix.

label: lem:mixed-trees
statement: Let $2\leq k\leq r$, put $R=r-k+1$, and suppose $\lambda_k\leq s$ with $s\geq1$. Choose nonnegative integers $p,q,u,v$ such that $p+q=k-2$ and $u+v=s-1$. Define \begin{equation} \begin{split} S={}&\binom{m+p}{p}\binom{R+u}{u}\\ &+\binom{m+q}{q}\binom{R+v}{v}-1. \end{split} \end{equation} If $n\geq\max\{m,S\}$, then $q_\lambda\leq K_n(\lambda)$ for either padding convention.

label: prop:short-second-row
statement: Let $\lambda\vdash nd$ have at most $n^2$ rows, put $t=\lambda_2\geq1$, $T=|\lambda|-\lambda_1$, and $k=\min\{d,T\}$. If \[ n\geq1+k(t-1), \] then $K_n(\lambda)$ equals the full ambient multiplicity. In particular the sufficient condition $n\geq1+(r-1)t(t-1)$ depends only on $r=\ell(\lambda)$ and the second row. One-row types also have full ambient multiplicity.

label: thm:criterion
title: Positive-padding criterion
statement: If $m<n$ and $c_m+3>2n^2+2$, then for every sufficiently large integer $d$ there is a partition $\lambda\vdash nd$ with exactly four nonzero parts such that \[ q_{m,n}(\lambda)>K_n(\lambda). \] No multiplicity obstruction of length at most three exists for any padded permanent.

label: thm:dimension
title: Quaternary permanent dimension
statement: For every integer $m\geq1$, \[ c_m=\min\left\{\binom{m+3}{3},\,4m^2-2m+2\right\}. \] Thus the map to quaternary forms is dominant exactly for $m\leq16$.

label: cor:range
statement: The criterion in Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion} first applies to $(m,n)=(8,9)$. For $m\geq17$ it applies exactly when \[ m<n,\qquad n^2\leq2m^2-m+1. \] Its asymptotic ratio has ceiling $\sqrt2$. This ceiling concerns the dimension argument; it is not an assertion excluding every multiplicity obstruction above that ratio.

label: thm:ray-comparison
title: Every fixed strict four-row direction
statement:
Let $m\geq3$, $n>m$, $a=n-m$, and let $
u\vdash ns$ have at most four parts, with trailing zeros appended, for a positive integer $s$. Suppose that $
u_4>0$ and $
u_1>as$. There is a positive real constant $c_
u$ such that \[  rac{q_{m,n}(j
u)}{K_n(j
u)} =c_
u j^{c_m-2n^2+1} igl(1+O(j^{-1}) igr) \qquad (j\longrightarrow\infty). \] Both multiplicities are positive for every sufficiently large integer $j$, and their coordinate degree is $sj$. Consequently the permanent multiplicity is eventually larger precisely when $c_m+3>2n^2+2$, provided that the two dimensions are unequal. If either $
u_4=0$ or $
u_1\leq as$, no stretch of this direction is a multiplicity obstruction.

label: thm:uniform-directions
statement: Fix $m\geq3$, $n>m$, $I\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$, and a compact subset $A\subset\Omega_I$. There are constants $c,C,D>0$ such that for every integer $d\geq D$ and every partition $\lambda\vdash nd$ with $\lambda/d\in A$, both multiplicities are positive and \[ c\,d^{\Delta}\ \leq\ \frac{q_{m,n}(\lambda)}{K_n(\lambda)} \ \leq C\,d^{\Delta},\qquad \Delta=c_m-2n^2+1. \] Consequently, if $\Delta<0$, one degree threshold excludes multiplicity obstructions throughout $A$. If $\Delta>0$, one threshold gives a multiplicity obstruction at every integral weight in $dA$.

label: cor:padding-strip
title: A strip along the padding face
statement: Let $1\leq m<n$, $d\geq0$, and let $\lambda\vdash nd$ have at most four parts. Then, in every size and degree, \[ \lambda_1\leq(n-m)d+3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_{m,n}(\lambda)\leq K_n(\lambda). \] The same inequality holds for the full variety of forms $\ell^{n-m}g$, with $g$ an arbitrary quaternary degree-$m$ form.

label: thm:quarticcontainment
title: A finite exclusion for quartics
statement: For every quaternary quartic $f$, every linear form $\ell$, and every $n\geq7$, \[ \ell^{n-4}f\in\mathcal D_{n,4}. \] Consequently, for the fourth permanent with an independent padding variable and every partition of length at most four, \[ q_{4,n}(\lambda)\leq K_n(\lambda)\qquad(n\geq7). \] The comparison holds in every coordinate degree and includes all copies of each irreducible representation.

label: thm:finite-nonic
title: A named finite multiplicity obstruction
statement: For every integer $s\geq0$, \begin{align*} q_{8,9}(s\lambda_0)&\geq\binom{s+155}{155},\\ K_9(s\lambda_0)&\leq \binom{9s+5}{5}\binom{9s+69}{69}\binom{9s+77}{77}. \end{align*} At $s=s_0$ the first bound is strictly larger than the second. Thus $s_0\lambda_0$ is a multiplicity obstruction in coordinate degree $27s_0=54\cdot10^{51}$.

label: thm:nonic-boxes
title: A complete nonic tail exclusion
statement: Let $d\geq0$ and let $\lambda\vdash9d$ have at most four nonzero parts, with trailing zeros appended. If \[ \lambda_2+\lambda_3+\lambda_4\leq32 \quad\text{or}\quad (\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4)\leq(19,7,7), \] then $K_9(\lambda)=a_{9,d}(\lambda)$. Consequently $q_{m,9}(\lambda)\leq K_9(\lambda)$ for every $1\leq m<9$: no padded permanent has a multiplicity obstruction at any such weight.

label: lem:restriction
title: Preservation of short-partition multiplicities
statement: For a degree-$n$ form $f$ in $N\geq r$ variables, let $Z_{f,r}$ be the closure of its arbitrary linear substitutions to $r$ variables. In every coordinate degree, the multiplicity of every partition of length at most $r$ is the same in $\C[\overline{\GL_Nf}]$ and $\C[Z_{f,r}]$.

label: lem:padding
title: Dimension of a positive linear-factor padding
statement: If $C$ is a nonzero irreducible affine cone of degree-$m$ forms in $r$ variables and $a>0$, the closure of $\{\ell^ag:g\in C,\ \ell\in(\C^r)^*\}$ has dimension $\dim C+r-1$.

label: lem:detdim
title: Determinantal dimension bound
statement: For every $n\geq1$, $\dim\mathcal D_{n,4}\leq2n^2+2$.

label: lem:ternary
title: Ternary saturation
statement: For $n\geq2$, every ternary degree-$n$ form lies in the orbit closure of $\det_n$. Consequently $K_n(\lambda)$ is the ambient plethysm multiplicity whenever $\ell(\lambda)\leq3$.

label: lem:perdimupper
title: Parameter bound
statement: For every $m\geq1$, $c_m\leq\min\{\binom{m+3}{3},4m^2-2m+2\}$.

label: prop:border
title: Bordered induction
statement: If some ternary data $A,u,v$ satisfy \begin{equation} \dim\mathcal C_A(u,v)=8m+2, \end{equation} then, with $c_m=\dim\mathcal P_{m,4}$, \begin{equation} c_{m+1}\geq c_m+8m+2. \end{equation}

label: lem:basecolumns
statement: For every $m\geq17$, some tridiagonal pencil $A_{ii}=\alpha_i x$, $A_{i,i+1}=y$, $A_{i+1,i}=\delta_i z$, with all $\alpha_i,\delta_i$ nonzero, and endpoint vectors $u=(x,0,\ldots,0,y)^t$, $v=(x,0,\ldots,0,z)^t$, satisfy $\dim\mathcal C_A(u,v)\geq8m-4$.

label: lem:endpointfull
statement: For every $m\geq17$, some ternary tridiagonal pencil $A$ and endpoint vectors $u,v$ of linear forms satisfy $\dim\mathcal C_A(u,v)=8m+2$.

label: lem:normal-coefficients
statement: For every $m\geq1$, the map $J_{m,3}$ is dominant. For $m\geq3$, its differential is surjective at the following explicit integral pencil. Put $N=2m$ and \[ c_i=(-1)^i\binom{N-1}{i-1},\qquad L_i=u+c_i(x+i y+i^2z)\quad(1\leq i\leq N). \] The pencil has diagonal entries $L_{2j-1}$, superdiagonal entries $L_{2j}$ for $1\leq j<m$, entry $L_{2m}$ in position $(m,1)$, and zero elsewhere.

label: cor:fourth-row-three
statement: For every $n\geq2$, $d\geq0$ and partition $\lambda\vdash nd$ with at most four rows and $\lambda_4\leq3$, \[ K_n(\lambda)=a_{n,d}(\lambda), \] where $a_{n,d}(\lambda)$ is the ambient plethysm multiplicity. Consequently no orbit closure of degree-$n$ forms can have a larger multiplicity at such a weight. In particular every positively padded permanent is excluded there.

label: lem:padding-face
title: A strip along the padding face
statement: Let $m<n$, $a=n-m$, $d\geq0$, and let $\lambda\vdash nd$ have at most four parts. If $\lambda_1<ad$, then $q_{m,n}(\lambda)=0$. In every size, \[ \lambda_1\leq ad+3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q_{m,n}(\lambda)\leq K_n(\lambda). \] The same conclusions hold with the padded permanent replaced by the full variety of forms $\ell^a g$, where $g$ is an arbitrary quaternary form of degree $m$.

label: cor:exact-eventual-boundary
title: Exact eventual boundary
statement: For $m\geq17$ and every fixed strict direction as in Theorem~\ref{thm:ray-comparison}, the permanent multiplicity is eventually larger when $n^2\leq2m^2-m+1$, and the determinant multiplicity is eventually larger when $n^2\geq2m^2-m+2$. In particular the latter conclusion holds for every $n>\sqrt2\,m$. For $3\leq m\leq16$, replace $2m^2-m+1$ by $\lfloor\binom{m+3}{3}/2\rfloor$ in the first alternative and use the complementary integer range for the second.

label: cor:boundary-depth
statement: Fix $m\geq3$, $n>m$, and a nonempty strict face $\Omega_I$. Set \[ E_P=c_m+r_I-13,\qquad E_D=2n^2+r_I-14. \] If $E_P<E_D$, there is a constant $C_I>0$ such that every multiplicity obstruction $\lambda\vdash nd$ with $\lambda/d\in\Omega_I$ satisfies \[ h_I(d,\lambda)\leq C_I d^{E_P/E_D}. \] In particular this holds for every $n>\sqrt2\,m$. The exponent is strictly less than one; the constant is not made effective.

label: prop:nonic-nested
statement: The projection of $\mathcal D_{9,4}$ to the coefficient space indexed by $J(b,c,e)$ is dominant if and only if $N(b,c,e)\leq164$. For every partition $\lambda\vdash9d$ of length at most four, put \[ (b,c,e)=\bigl(\min(9,\lambda_2),\min(9,\lambda_3), \min(9,\lambda_4)\bigr). \] If $N(b,c,e)\leq164$, then $K_9(\lambda)=a_{9,d}(\lambda)$. In particular this equality holds whenever $\lambda_4\leq3$, and also whenever $\lambda_3\leq6$ and $\lambda_4\leq5$.

label: prop:first-eight-hypersurface
statement: The variety $Z_8$ is an irreducible hypersurface. Its irreducible defining polynomial is a $\GL_3$ semi-invariant of character $\det^c$ for a positive integer $c$, in the polynomial-action convention used here. It is invariant under the translations $A_i\mapsto A_i+a_iI$ and can therefore be written in the centered coefficient tensors of orders two through eight. The induced map from the simultaneous-conjugation quotient is not finite.

label: prop:first-eight-weight-bound
statement: The character exponent of the first-eight hypersurface satisfies $c\geq256$.

label: cor:first-eight-homogenization
statement: Let $D$ be the ordinary total degree of $G$ in its $164$ coefficient variables. Its minimal homogenization \[ P_G(F)=F_0^D\, G\left((F_\alpha/F_0)_{1\leq|\alpha|\leq8}\right) \] is a nonzero highest-weight equation for the quaternary size-nine determinant closure, of coordinate degree $D$ and weight \[ (9D-3c,c,c,c). \] Consequently $9D\geq4c$, and in particular $D\geq114$. This conclusion concerns the homogenization of this generator.

label: thm:normal-weight-eleven
title: Normal weight eleven
statement: For every $d\geq0$ and every partition $\lambda\vdash9d$ of length at most four with $\lambda_4\leq11$, \[ K_9(\lambda)=a_{9,d}(\lambda). \] Thus no such partition is a multiplicity obstruction against the size-nine determinant, including for the independently once-padded permanent of size eight.

label: lem:normal-weight-leading-term
statement: Suppose $f_1:V\longrightarrow W_1$ is a surjective linear map and $f_j:V\longrightarrow W_j$ is homogeneous of degree $j$ for $2\leq j\leq s$. Put $L=\ker f_1$ and $g_j=f_j|_L$. If substitution by $g_2,\ldots,g_s$ is injective on every formal weighted homogeneous polynomial space of weight at most $s$, then substitution by $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ has the same property.

label: lem:finite-normal-quadratics
title: Finite quadratic parameters
statement: For every $m\geq2$, there is a nonempty Zariski-open set of ternary $m$-square pencils on which \[ F_1(D,-):\operatorname{Mat}_m\longrightarrow\Sym^{m-1}\C^3 \] is surjective. Its kernel $K_D$ has dimension $s=\binom m2$, and the homogeneous quadratic map \[ q_D=F_2(D,-)|_{K_D}:K_D\longrightarrow\Sym^{m-2}\C^3 \] is finite. In particular its $s$ coefficient functions are a homogeneous system of parameters in $\C[K_D]$.

label: lem:normal-free-summands
title: Lifting residue classes to free summands
statement: Let $D$ belong to the open set of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-normal-quadratics}, and write \[ R=\C[K_D],\qquad B=\C[q_1,\ldots,q_s],\qquad A=R/(q_1,\ldots,q_s), \] where the $q_i$ are the coefficient functions of $F_2$. Then $B$ is a polynomial ring, each $q_i$ has degree two, and $R$ is a finite graded free $B$-module. Any homogeneous polynomials whose classes are linearly independent in $A$ can be included, unchanged, in a homogeneous free $B$-basis of $R$.

label: lem:weighted-skew-kernel
title: A regular kernel degeneration
statement: Fix $m\geq2$, index vertices by $0,\ldots,m-1$, and put \[ L_i=x+iy+i^2z,\qquad D_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(L_i)+\varepsilon zB, \] where $B_{ii}=0$ and every $B_{ij}$ with $i\ne j$ is nonzero. Over $\C(\varepsilon)$ the first normal map has full rank $\binom{m+1}{2}$. Its kernel has a basis regular at $\varepsilon=0$, with upper entries $H_{ij}=u_{ij}$ free and limiting matrix \begin{equation} H^0_{ii}=0,\qquad H^0_{ij}=u_{ij},\qquad H^0_{ji}=-\rho_{ij}u_{ij},\qquad \rho_{ij}=B_{ji}/B_{ij}\quad(i<j). \end{equation} In these coordinates the limiting second normal coefficients are an invertible linear transform of the squares $u_{ij}^2$.

label: thm:universal-normal-five
statement: For every $n\geq2$, $d\geq0$ and partition $\lambda\vdash nd$ with at most four parts and $\lambda_4\leq5$, \[ K_n(\lambda)=a_{n,d}(\lambda), \qquad a_{n,d}(\lambda)=[S_\lambda\C^4]\Sym^d(\Sym^n\C^4). \] Consequently no orbit closure of degree-$n$ forms has a larger multiplicity at such a weight. In particular this excludes every positively padded permanent in this region.

label: thm:universal-normal-six
statement: For every $n\geq5$, $d\geq0$, and partition $\lambda\vdash nd$ with at most four parts and $\lambda_4\leq6$, \[ K_n(\lambda)=a_{n,d}(\lambda). \] Consequently no padded permanent, or other orbit closure of a degree-$n$ form, has larger multiplicity at such a weight.

label: lem:universal-six-cubic-kernel
statement: For $n\geq4$, the kernel of the complete quadratic product map from the formal cubic coefficient space to $A_6$ has the independent basis $\{C_e^2:e\in E\}$. If $n\geq6$, adjoining all coefficients of $G_6$ introduces no further relation. Thus the kernel on $G_6\oplus\Sym^2(G_3)$ is the same space, with $G_6$ omitted when $n<6$.

label: lem:universal-six-quartic-repair
statement: For every $n\geq5$, a nonempty open set of distinct rational parameters $t_i$ makes the classes of the complete list $G_4$ and all $\binom n2$ polynomials $T_e$ jointly independent in $A_4$.

statement:
